questions.prompt: How should problems be prioritized for analysis in problem control?
choices: According to which team reported the related incidents
Based on the risk they pose, considering impact and probability
In the order the problems were identified
According to how many staff are available to investigate
questions.explanation: Problems are prioritized according to risk so effort is focused where it matters most.

questions.prompt: Why is a workaround documented in a problem record?
choices: So the service desk no longer needs to be involved
Because a workaround removes the need for any resolution
So the problem record can be closed straight away
So it can be reused for related incidents and reviewed and improved over time
questions.explanation: Documented workarounds speed incident resolution and are reassessed during error control.

questions.prompt: A known error has a workaround, and a permanent fix is too costly compared with its impact. What may be appropriate?
choices: Raise an emergency change to apply the costly fix immediately
Close all related incidents and the problem without further action
Continue using the workaround and keep the known error under review
Delete the known error record since no fix is planned
questions.explanation: When a permanent fix is not justified, an effective workaround may be retained while the known error is periodically reassessed.

questions.prompt: Which practice is most closely involved when problem management identifies a permanent solution that requires modifying a live system?
choices: Service request management
Relationship management
Change enablement
Supplier management
questions.explanation: Permanent fixes are usually implemented through a change request handled by change enablement.

questions.prompt: How do incident management and problem management differ?
choices: Incident management restores service quickly, while problem management investigates and manages underlying causes
They are the same practice described under two different names
Problem management deals with hardware, incident management with software
Incident management finds root causes, while problem management restores service
questions.explanation: The two practices are closely linked but have different objectives and timescales.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of the service request management practice?
choices: To capture demand for incident resolution and service requests, and act as the entry point and single point of contact for the service provider with all its users
To set clear business-based targets for service levels and ensure delivery of services is properly assessed, monitored and managed against these targets
To minimize the negative impact of incidents by restoring normal service operation as quickly as possible
To support the agreed quality of a service by handling all predefined, user-initiated service requests in an effective and user-friendly manner
questions.explanation: Service request management handles the normal, expected requests that are part of service delivery.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a typical service request?
choices: A request for access to a shared folder
A report that the email system is down
A high-risk upgrade to a core system
An investigation into recurring network failures
questions.explanation: Requests for access, information, resources or service actions are service requests; outages are incidents.

questions.prompt: How should service requests be handled wherever possible?
choices: Only by senior engineers
With a fresh assessment by a change board each time
Only through walk-in support
Using standardized and automated workflows
questions.explanation: Because requests are predefined, they can be standardized and automated to improve efficiency.

questions.prompt: Which statement about service requests and approvals is correct?
choices: Approvals for service requests are always handled by suppliers
Every service request must be approved by the sponsor before fulfilment
Policies should define which requests can be fulfilled with limited or no additional approvals
Service requests are pre-defined, so approvals are never needed
questions.explanation: Clear policies streamline fulfilment while maintaining appropriate control.

questions.prompt: A user submits a compliment about excellent support received. How might this be handled?
choices: As an incident with low priority
As a problem for later analysis
As a normal change to the service
As a type of service request covering feedback, compliments and complaints
questions.explanation: Feedback, compliments and complaints can be handled within service request management.

questions.prompt: A user asks for information on how to configure a printer. Which practice should handle this?
choices: Deployment management
Problem management
Service request management
Change enablement
questions.explanation: A request for information is a typical service request.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of the service desk practice?
choices: To support the agreed quality of a service by handling all predefined, user-initiated service requests in an effective and user-friendly manner
To minimize the negative impact of incidents by restoring normal service operation as quickly as possible
To establish and nurture the links between the organization and its stakeholders at strategic and tactical levels
To capture demand for incident resolution and service requests, and act as the entry point and single point of contact for the service provider with all its users
questions.explanation: The service desk is the user-facing point of contact for incidents and requests.

questions.prompt: Which skills does ITIL 4 emphasize most for service desk staff?
choices: Deep specialist expertise in every technology
Software development
Empathy and effective communication with users
Contract negotiation
questions.explanation: The service desk focuses on understanding users and the business context, not necessarily deep technical skill.

questions.prompt: Which statement about service desk channels is correct?
choices: Users should be encouraged to attend in person for faster resolution
Telephone should be the only channel so that requests can be tracked
Service desks may use phone, email, chat, service portals, walk-in and social media channels
Email and chat should be avoided because they cannot be prioritized
questions.explanation: Modern service desks provide multiple channels to suit users' needs.

questions.prompt: Staff in several countries and time zones work together as one service desk using shared tools. What is this arrangement called?
choices: A change advisory board
A virtual service desk
A walk-in service desk
A swarming team
questions.explanation: A virtual service desk lets geographically dispersed staff operate as a single team.

questions.prompt: Which tool supports the service desk in resolving issues quickly at first contact?
choices: A change schedule
A continual improvement register
A supplier contract database
A knowledge base
questions.explanation: Knowledge bases help staff find solutions and workarounds quickly.

questions.prompt: What does ITIL 4 say about the service desk's understanding of the organization?
choices: The service desk should focus on closing tickets rather than business context
The service desk mainly needs deep technical knowledge of the infrastructure
Business knowledge is the concern of relationship managers, not the service desk
The service desk should understand the wider organization, business processes and users
questions.explanation: Understanding the business context helps the service desk support users and prioritize effectively.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of the service level management practice?
choices: To align the organization's practices and services with changing business needs through ongoing improvement
To establish and nurture the links between the organization and its stakeholders at strategic and tactical levels
To ensure that the organization's suppliers and their performance are managed appropriately to support the seamless provision of quality products and services
To set clear business-based targets for service levels and ensure delivery of services is properly assessed, monitored and managed against these targets
questions.explanation: Service level management defines and tracks service performance against business-based targets.

questions.prompt: What is a service level agreement (SLA)?
choices: A description of a known error together with its documented workaround
A record of all changes that have been authorized for the coming month
A contract between a service provider and its hardware supplier covering delivery times
A documented agreement between a service provider and a customer that identifies both services required and the expected level of service
questions.explanation: SLAs capture agreed services and service levels between provider and customer.

questions.prompt: A provider's SLA reports show all targets met, yet customers complain about poor service. What is this situation often called?
choices: The watermelon SLA effect
Shift-left
Error control
Swarming
questions.explanation: Like a watermelon, reports look green outside while customers experience red inside, often because metrics are too narrow.

questions.prompt: Which characteristic makes an SLA more effective?
choices: It includes outcome-based metrics that reflect the customer's experience
It focuses on technical metrics such as server uptime
It uses detailed technical language for precision
It is written by the provider without customer involvement
questions.explanation: SLAs should be related to defined services, simply written and include metrics that reflect business outcomes.

questions.prompt: Which activity helps service level management understand what customers value?
choices: Running deployment pipelines for new releases
Analysing configuration item records and their relationships
Reviewing supplier invoices against contract terms
Customer engagement, such as listening and asking about their business needs
questions.explanation: Engaging with customers to understand their needs is key to setting meaningful service levels.

questions.prompt: Which source of information is used by service level management?
choices: The change schedule and the record of authorized changes
Configuration records held in the configuration management system
Customer feedback, operational metrics and business metrics
Supplier contracts and their associated penalty clauses
questions.explanation: A combination of feedback and metrics gives a complete picture of service performance.

questions.prompt: Which skills are most relevant for service level management?
choices: Software coding and automated testing
Network cabling and hardware repair
Accounting and payroll administration
Relationship management, business liaison and business analysis
questions.explanation: Service level management relies on understanding customers and translating needs into targets.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of the information security management practice?
choices: To plan and manage the full lifecycle of all IT assets to maximize value, control costs, manage risks and support decisions about purchase, reuse and retirement
To protect the information needed by the organization to conduct its business
To systematically observe services and service components, and record and report selected changes of state identified as events
To ensure that accurate and reliable information about the configuration of services, and the configuration items that support them, is available when and where needed
questions.explanation: Information security management addresses confidentiality, integrity and availability of information, among other aspects.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of the relationship management practice?
choices: To capture demand for incident resolution and service requests, and act as the entry point and single point of contact for the service provider with all its users
To establish and nurture the links between the organization and its stakeholders at strategic and tactical levels
To ensure that the organization's suppliers and their performance are managed appropriately to support the seamless provision of quality products and services
To set clear business-based targets for service levels and ensure delivery of services is properly assessed, monitored and managed against these targets
questions.explanation: Relationship management builds and maintains stakeholder relationships.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of the supplier management practice?
choices: To set clear business-based targets for service levels and ensure delivery of services is properly assessed, monitored and managed against these targets
To establish and nurture the links between the organization and its stakeholders at strategic and tactical levels
To ensure that the organization's suppliers and their performance are managed appropriately to support the seamless provision of quality products and services
To plan and manage the full lifecycle of all IT assets to maximize value, control costs, manage risks and support decisions about purchase, reuse and retirement
questions.explanation: Supplier management focuses on managing suppliers and their performance.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of the IT asset management practice?
choices: To plan and manage the full lifecycle of all IT assets to maximize value, control costs, manage risks and support decisions about purchase, reuse and retirement
To ensure that the organization's suppliers and their performance are managed appropriately to support the seamless provision of quality products and services
To ensure that accurate and reliable information about the configuration of services, and the configuration items that support them, is available when and where needed
To move new or changed hardware, software, documentation, processes or any other component to live environments
questions.explanation: IT asset management covers assets from acquisition to disposal and supports regulatory and contractual compliance.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of the monitoring and event management practice?
choices: To reduce the likelihood and impact of incidents by identifying actual and potential causes of incidents and managing workarounds and known errors
To minimize the negative impact of incidents by restoring normal service operation as quickly as possible
To ensure that accurate and reliable information about the configuration of services, and the configuration items that support them, is available when and where needed
To systematically observe services and service components, and record and report selected changes of state identified as events
questions.explanation: Monitoring and event management detects and records significant changes of state.

questions.prompt: How does ITIL 4 define an event?
choices: A request from a user that initiates a service action agreed as normal
Any change of state that has significance for the management of a service or other configuration item
An unplanned interruption to a service or reduction in the quality of a service
A scheduled modification to a configuration item approved by a change authority
questions.explanation: Events can be informational, warnings or exceptions, and some may lead to incidents.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of the release management practice?
choices: To maximize the number of successful service and product changes by ensuring risks are properly assessed, authorizing changes and managing the change schedule
To move new or changed hardware, software, documentation, processes or any other component to live environments
To make new and changed services and features available for use
To protect the information needed by the organization to conduct its business
questions.explanation: Release management controls when new functionality becomes available to users.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of the service configuration management practice?
choices: To systematically observe services and service components, and record and report selected changes of state identified as events
To maximize the number of successful service and product changes by ensuring risks are properly assessed, authorizing changes and managing the change schedule
To ensure that accurate and reliable information about the configuration of services, and the configuration items that support them, is available when and where needed
To plan and manage the full lifecycle of all IT assets to maximize value, control costs, manage risks and support decisions about purchase, reuse and retirement
questions.explanation: Service configuration management maintains information about CIs and their relationships.

questions.prompt: How does ITIL 4 define a configuration item (CI)?
choices: Any change of state that has significance for the management of a service
Any component that needs to be managed in order to deliver an IT service
Any user or customer who is registered to consume an IT service
Any financially valuable component that can contribute to delivering an IT product or service
questions.explanation: CIs include hardware, software, documentation and other components whose configuration must be controlled.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of the deployment management practice?
choices: To maximize the number of successful service and product changes by ensuring risks are properly assessed, authorizing changes and managing the change schedule
To make new and changed services and features available for use
To move new or changed hardware, software, documentation, processes or any other component to live environments
To ensure that accurate and reliable information about the configuration of services, and the configuration items that support them, is available when and where needed
questions.explanation: Deployment management handles moving components into live (and sometimes other) environments, separate from releasing them to users.

questions.prompt: A new feature is deployed to production but hidden behind a feature flag until the marketing launch, when it is switched on for users. Which practices handle the deployment and the launch respectively?
choices: Deployment management and release management
Change enablement and service request management
Service configuration management and IT asset management
Release management and deployment management
questions.explanation: Deployment moves the component to the live environment; release makes it available for use.

questions.prompt: How does ITIL 4 define an IT asset?
choices: Any document that describes the utility and warranty of a service
Any component that needs to be managed in order to deliver an IT service
Any change of state that has significance for the management of a service
Any financially valuable component that can contribute to the delivery of an IT product or service
questions.explanation: IT assets are defined by financial value; CIs are defined by the need to manage them for service delivery.

questions.prompt: A customer says a new HR portal is 'fit for purpose' but not 'fit for use'. What does this mean?
choices: It is cheap to run but expensive for the customer to adopt
It meets the SLA but has not yet been formally released
It has the right features but does not perform reliably enough
It performs reliably but lacks the features the customer needs
questions.explanation: Fit for purpose describes utility (functionality); fit for use describes warranty (meeting agreed performance such as availability and capacity).

questions.prompt: Which of the following is the BEST example of utility?
choices: A guarantee that the service is available during business hours
A plan to recover the service after a major site failure
Enough capacity to support the peak number of concurrent users
A feature that removes a constraint the user previously faced
questions.explanation: Utility is about functionality: supporting the consumer's performance or removing constraints. Availability, continuity and capacity are aspects of warranty.

questions.prompt: An online store adds a second data centre so that checkout keeps working if one site fails. What is being improved?
choices: Utility, through new checkout functionality
Warranty, through improved service continuity
The sponsor role, through a new budget approval
The service offering, through new goods
questions.explanation: Continuity is an aspect of warranty: the assurance that the service will meet agreed requirements even when things go wrong.

questions.prompt: A provider gives a consumer a set of laptops that the consumer then owns and is responsible for. Which part of a service offering is this?
choices: Access to resources, because the consumer can use them
Goods, because ownership is transferred to the consumer
Warranty, because the laptops must work reliably
A service action, because the laptops are delivered
questions.explanation: Goods are supplied with ownership transferred to the consumer, who then takes responsibility for their future use.

questions.prompt: A company rents capacity on a provider's storage platform. It can store files there but never owns the hardware. What is this an example of?
choices: A service action
A service relationship model
Goods
Access to resources
questions.explanation: Access to resources grants the consumer use of resources under agreed terms without transferring ownership.

questions.prompt: Which statement BEST describes how value is perceived in ITIL 4?
choices: It equals the price the consumer pays, less the provider's delivery cost
It is subjective and can differ between stakeholders of the same service
It is the same for every consumer of a given service
It is fixed by the provider when the service is designed and documented
questions.explanation: Value is the perceived benefits, usefulness and importance of something, so different stakeholders can see different value in the same service.

questions.prompt: From a provider's point of view, which is a typical form of value received from a service relationship?
choices: Lower risk because the consumer runs the infrastructure
Funding from the consumer and business development opportunities
Removal of costs the provider previously carried for its own infrastructure
Outcomes the consumer achieves using the service
questions.explanation: Providers typically gain funding, business development and image improvement from service relationships; outcomes and removed costs are value for the consumer.

questions.prompt: A bank introduces an online loan application. Which is the outcome rather than the output?
choices: A decision report generated for each application
A new web form for submitting loan applications
Customers obtain approved loans faster than before
A confirmation email sent to each applicant
questions.explanation: Outputs are deliverables of an activity, such as forms, reports and emails; the outcome is the result the stakeholder wants, such as obtaining loans faster.

questions.prompt: Which role is MOST likely to take responsibility for the outcomes of service consumption in a large organization?
choices: The customer
The sponsor
The user
The supplier
questions.explanation: The customer defines requirements and takes responsibility for the outcomes of service consumption; the sponsor authorizes budget and the user uses the service.

questions.prompt: A school buys a learning platform. The head teacher approves the spending, the IT lead defines requirements, and pupils log in to study. Which role do the pupils hold?
choices: User
Sponsor
Service provider
Customer
questions.explanation: Users are the people who actually use the services; the customer defines requirements and the sponsor authorizes budget.

questions.prompt: What does ITIL 4 mean when it says a service provider takes on 'specific costs and risks' for the consumer?
choices: The consumer no longer manages certain costs and risks itself
The consumer pays nothing and bears no risk at all
The provider accepts every cost and risk the consumer previously had
The provider shares its profits and losses with the consumer
questions.explanation: A service removes some costs and risks from the consumer, but the consumer still bears other costs and risks, such as fees and dependency on the provider.

questions.prompt: Which statement about costs in a service relationship is correct?
choices: Only the provider incurs costs when a service is delivered
Costs are not part of value and can be ignored by the consumer when choosing
A service can both remove some costs and impose new costs on the consumer
A service always reduces the total cost to the consumer over its lifetime
questions.explanation: Consumers evaluate both costs removed (such as staff or infrastructure) and costs imposed (such as fees, training and integration).

questions.prompt: When a consumer evaluates a new service, what should it weigh against the outcomes it expects?
choices: The costs and risks the service removes and the ones it introduces
Only the provider's reputation in the market
Only the number of features the provider offers compared with competitors
Only the purchase price stated in the contract and any discounts offered
questions.explanation: Value depends on balancing desired outcomes against both the costs and risks taken away and those that are imposed.

questions.prompt: Which statement about the relationship between products and services is correct?
choices: Services are based on one or more products
A product and a service are the same thing in ITIL 4
Services can be offered without any product behind them
Products are based on one or more services
questions.explanation: Organizations configure their resources into products, and services are offered to consumers based on one or more of those products.

questions.prompt: Why might a consumer not see most of the components of a product?
choices: Providers are required to hide all product details by contract
Products contain only intangible elements that cannot be seen
Products are complex and often only partly visible to consumers
Consumers are not allowed to know which provider supplies the product
questions.explanation: Products are typically complex configurations of resources, and the consumer usually sees only the parts that matter to the service they receive.

questions.prompt: A provider offers the same core product to two groups: a basic package for small firms and a premium package with extra support for enterprises. What are these packages?
choices: Two value streams for the same service action
Two service relationships with the same sponsor
Two separate products built from different sets of resources
Different service offerings based on the same product
questions.explanation: Service offerings are formal descriptions of services tailored to target consumer groups, and several can be built from one product.

questions.prompt: In a service relationship, which activity is the responsibility of the service consumer?
choices: Configuring the provider's own resources so that the service can be delivered
Managing the consumer's own resources needed to consume the service
Authorizing changes to the provider's infrastructure
Designing the provider's service offerings and pricing
questions.explanation: Service consumption includes managing the consumer's resources needed to use the service, as well as using it and requesting service actions.

questions.prompt: An organization relies on an external payroll provider while also running its own internal IT services for staff. Which statement is correct?
choices: It must merge both relationships into a single service level agreement
It can only be classed as a provider of services
It acts as a consumer in one relationship and a provider in another
It can only be classed as a consumer because it buys external services
questions.explanation: Organizations commonly act as both service consumers and service providers, forming chains of service relationships.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is an example of a service action?
choices: A sponsor approving next year's service budget
A user owning the headset supplied with a contract
A support engineer resetting a user's multi-factor authentication
A user storing project files on the provider's cloud storage platform
questions.explanation: Service actions are performed by the provider to address consumer needs, such as user support; ownership of goods and use of storage are other offering elements.

questions.prompt: Which aspect of warranty is MOST affected when a service slows down badly because too many users log in at once?
choices: Continuity
Security
Utility
Capacity
questions.explanation: Capacity is an aspect of warranty; when demand exceeds capacity, performance falls below agreed levels even though the functions still exist.

questions.prompt: A provider launches a service that has excellent features but frequent security breaches. Why is the service unlikely to create value?
choices: Security is part of utility, so the service's features are considered faulty
Value is only created when the consumer bears no additional costs or risks
A service with good utility never needs warranty to create value
Without adequate warranty, the utility cannot be relied on to deliver outcomes
questions.explanation: Both utility and warranty are needed; poor security (warranty) undermines the consumer's ability to achieve outcomes from the functionality.

questions.prompt: What is the MAIN purpose of the service relationship management activities in a service relationship?
choices: To transfer ownership of goods from the provider to the consumer's organization
To configure provider resources into new products
To authorize the budget for consuming the service
To ensure continued value co-creation based on the agreed offerings
questions.explanation: Service relationship management covers joint activities by provider and consumer to keep value co-creation going.

questions.prompt: Which stakeholder would MOST typically value a provider through employment, taxes and organizational contributions to the community?
choices: Shareholders
Partners and suppliers
Society and community
Service consumers
questions.explanation: Society and the community gain value such as employment, taxes and contributions from service providers; shareholders seek financial benefits.

questions.prompt: A provider and consumer agree that the consumer will supply accurate data and timely approvals for a service to work well. What does this illustrate?
choices: The service has no warranty until the data is supplied
The consumer has become the service provider
Value is co-created and depends on both parties contributing
The provider has transferred all its risks to the consumer
questions.explanation: Value co-creation means consumers are active participants, contributing resources such as information and approvals.

questions.prompt: Which statement about outcomes is correct?
choices: An outcome is the same as an output
An outcome is always a tangible deliverable
An outcome can be enabled by one or more outputs
An outcome is produced only by the service provider
questions.explanation: Outcomes are results for stakeholders enabled by outputs; outputs are the deliverables of activities.

questions.prompt: In ITIL 4, what does service management focus on enabling?
choices: Delivery of IT projects within budget
The lowest possible cost for the provider
Value for customers in the form of services
Maximum utilization of technical resources
questions.explanation: Service management is a set of specialized organizational capabilities for enabling value for customers in the form of services.

questions.prompt: A user complains a service 'does exactly what we need but keeps crashing'. A manager says 'it is reliable but cannot do what we need'. Which aspects are they criticising, respectively?
choices: Utility and warranty
Outputs and outcomes
Costs and risks
Warranty and utility
questions.explanation: Crashing despite correct functions is a warranty issue; reliability without needed functions is a utility issue.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is considered a risk REMOVED from a consumer by using a service?
choices: The provider failing to meet its security obligations
The consumer losing internal skills it once had to run the servers
Failure of on-premises servers the consumer previously had to maintain
The provider going out of business part way through the contract term
questions.explanation: Using a service can remove risks such as failure of consumer-owned infrastructure, while introducing new risks such as provider dependency.

questions.prompt: A project team keeps adding new features without checking whether users want them. Which guiding principle would MOST help redirect their effort?
choices: Start where you are
Focus on value
Think and work holistically
Optimize and automate
questions.explanation: Focus on value asks that everything the organization does links back to value for stakeholders, so work should be driven by what users actually need.

questions.prompt: When applying 'focus on value', why is the user experience important?
choices: User experience only matters for consumer-facing websites and mobile apps
User experience is measured only by the service desk
Experience is part of how consumers judge the value of a service
User experience replaces the need to measure outcomes
questions.explanation: Customer and user experience are significant parts of perceived value, so they must be understood and managed along with outcomes.

questions.prompt: A service provider applies 'focus on value' for internal IT. Who should it identify as the service consumer?
choices: Only the suppliers who provide the technology
The business units and staff who use and pay for the services
Only the IT staff who support the services
Only the external customers who buy the organization's own products
questions.explanation: Focus on value starts with knowing who the consumers are; for internal IT these are the business units and users it serves.

questions.prompt: An organization plans to replace its change process. Before designing anything new, the team reviews the existing process to find what still works. Which principle is this?
choices: Focus on value
Progress iteratively with feedback
Start where you are
Keep it simple and practical
questions.explanation: Start where you are encourages assessing the current state and reusing what is valuable before building something new.

questions.prompt: Under 'start where you are', why should existing services and processes be considered for reuse?
choices: Reusing what works reduces waste and risk compared with starting over
Reuse is required by every governance framework
Existing services must always be kept unchanged
Existing services are always better than new ones and should be protected
questions.explanation: Discarding everything and starting over is wasteful and risky; much of the current state is often reusable or can be improved.

questions.prompt: A team relies only on reports to judge a process, but the reports contain old data. What does 'start where you are' recommend?
choices: Supplement the measurements with direct observation
Assume the reports are accurate and continue the plan
Rebuild the reports before any improvement is planned
Stop measuring and rely on staff opinions instead
questions.explanation: Measurement supports analysis, but data can be misleading or out of date, so direct observation helps understand the real current state.

questions.prompt: A team delivers a large change all at once and finds months later that it no longer meets needs. Which principle could have prevented this?
choices: Collaborate and promote visibility
Progress iteratively with feedback
Optimize and automate
Start where you are
questions.explanation: Breaking work into smaller iterations with feedback lets teams detect changing needs early and adjust direction.

questions.prompt: When progressing iteratively, what is a feedback loop used for?
choices: Returning faulty products to the supplier for repair
Using outputs and results of one part of the work to adjust what follows
Escalating incidents back to the service desk
Sending approved changes back to the change authority for a final review
questions.explanation: A feedback loop occurs when outputs of part of a system are used as inputs to that part, allowing actions to be adjusted based on results.

questions.prompt: A team is so focused on gathering feedback that it never completes any iteration. What does ITIL 4 advise?
choices: The team should stop iterating and plan the whole initiative upfront instead
Feedback is important, but iterations must still progress and deliver
Feedback should be collected only from managers
Feedback should be ignored until the final release
questions.explanation: Progress iteratively with feedback warns against analysis paralysis: feedback should inform progress, not prevent it.

questions.prompt: Which statement BEST reflects 'progress iteratively with feedback' when circumstances change during an initiative?
choices: Changes should be postponed until the initiative is complete
The initiative should be cancelled and restarted
The original plan should be followed without deviation
The approach can be revised in the next iteration
questions.explanation: Each iteration provides an opportunity to reevaluate and adjust the work to reflect new circumstances.

questions.prompt: An improvement team designs a new process without involving the people who will use it, and adoption is poor. Which principle was MOST neglected?
choices: Collaborate and promote visibility
Optimize and automate
Keep it simple and practical
Start where you are
questions.explanation: Involving the right stakeholders builds buy-in and relevance; without collaboration, initiatives often fail to be adopted.

questions.prompt: According to 'collaborate and promote visibility', why should the work and its progress be made visible?
choices: So stakeholders can support it and make informed decisions
So suppliers can bid for the work being performed
So auditors can approve each task before it is allowed to start
So managers can monitor individual staff productivity
questions.explanation: Visibility of work supports good decisions, reduces hidden agendas and builds support for improvement.

questions.prompt: Which statement about collaboration in ITIL 4 is correct?
choices: It replaces the need for clear roles and responsibilities
It means that every decision requires full consensus
It should be limited to people within the same department
It can include people outside the team, such as customers
questions.explanation: Collaborate and promote visibility encourages involving the right stakeholders, including customers, users and suppliers where useful.

questions.prompt: A team is reluctant to involve a sceptical stakeholder group in an improvement. What does ITIL 4 suggest?
choices: Engaging critics early can improve the outcome and build support
Sceptical groups should be replaced by supportive ones
Sceptical groups should be excluded to avoid delays
Sceptical groups should only be informed after the improvement is completed
questions.explanation: Collaboration is about involving the right people; even sceptics can contribute insight and become supporters when engaged.

questions.prompt: An organization optimizes its service desk in isolation, but the change overloads second-line teams. Which principle was ignored?
choices: Focus on value
Progress iteratively with feedback
Think and work holistically
Optimize and automate
questions.explanation: Think and work holistically recognizes that outcomes depend on how all parts of the system work together, not on one part alone.

questions.prompt: When applying 'think and work holistically', which approach to automation is recommended?
choices: Automation can help, especially where it supports integration
Automation should be avoided because it tends to isolate teams
Automation should replace analysis of system interactions
Automation should only be applied by external suppliers
questions.explanation: Holistic working is facilitated by automation where it supports end-to-end integration and visibility across the system.

questions.prompt: Which statement BEST expresses 'think and work holistically'?
choices: Outcomes depend on how all the elements of the system work together
Each team should optimize its own work independently
Technology is the main factor that determines success
A single practice should be fully optimized before any other is considered
questions.explanation: Services are delivered through the integrated work of many teams, practices, partners and technologies.

questions.prompt: A team creates a 40-step process when 10 steps would achieve the same result. Which principle is MOST relevant?
choices: Keep it simple and practical
Think and work holistically
Collaborate and promote visibility
Start where you are
questions.explanation: Keep it simple and practical recommends using the minimum number of steps needed to achieve the objective.

questions.prompt: When applying 'keep it simple and practical', what should be done with a control that adds no value but is required by regulation?
choices: Document it but ignore it in daily operations
Keep it, because it is needed to meet a compliance obligation
Remove it, because it does not add value for the service consumer
Automate it fully so that no one has to review it
questions.explanation: Simplicity is about removing what does not contribute to value or required outcomes; compliance requirements still have to be met.

questions.prompt: What does ITIL 4 suggest about designing a process for every exception?
choices: Exceptions should be forbidden so that the process always stays simple
Exceptions should be automated before the main process
Design for the common cases and handle rare exceptions separately
Every exception should have its own documented workflow
questions.explanation: Trying to cover every exception produces overly complex processes; rules should be designed for the normal situation.

questions.prompt: A process improvement removes several approvals and introduces quick wins that customers notice immediately. Which principle is MOST clearly applied?
choices: Optimize and automate
Keep it simple and practical
Start where you are
Think and work holistically
questions.explanation: Removing unnecessary steps and delivering quick wins that show progress are both associated with keep it simple and practical.

questions.prompt: Which statement about 'keep it simple and practical' and understanding value is correct?
choices: Value should be ignored when deciding what to simplify
Knowing how each element contributes to value helps decide what to keep
Simplicity is more important than the outcomes achieved
All existing elements must be kept because they were approved by management
questions.explanation: Understanding contributions to value is how a team decides which steps, controls and outputs to keep or remove.

questions.prompt: A manager wants to automate a process to fix its problems. What should be done FIRST according to ITIL 4?
choices: Select an automation tool and configure it immediately
Optimize and simplify the process as far as practical
Hire extra staff to run the process in parallel
Outsource the process to a specialist supplier
questions.explanation: Optimize and automate recommends simplifying and optimizing before automating, so that inefficiencies are not built into the automation.

questions.prompt: Which statement BEST describes the purpose of optimization in ITIL 4?
choices: To reduce the number of staff in every team
To make every process as fast as technically possible
To replace manual work with automation wherever it is possible to do so
To make something as effective and useful as it needs to be
questions.explanation: Optimization means making something as effective and useful as it needs to be, which comes before any decision to automate.

questions.prompt: What is the main benefit of automating frequent and repetitive tasks?
choices: It guarantees that no errors will occur in the process
It eliminates the need for any human decision-making
It removes the need to measure the outcomes of those tasks in future
Staff can be freed to focus on more complex and valuable work
questions.explanation: Automation of standard, repeatable tasks increases efficiency and frees human resources for work where they add value.

questions.prompt: Which step should come early when optimizing a process, according to ITIL 4?
choices: Choose the vendor that will supply the automation tool
Assess the current state of the proposed optimization
Remove all approvals to make the process faster
Automate the process before measuring its performance
questions.explanation: The optimization approach includes understanding the context, assessing the current state, agreeing the future state, and ensuring stakeholder engagement.

questions.prompt: Which pair of guiding principles is MOST directly applied when a team first assesses a process and then simplifies it?
choices: Collaborate and promote visibility, and think and work holistically
Focus on value, and optimize and automate
Progress iteratively with feedback, and focus on value
Start where you are, and keep it simple and practical
questions.explanation: Assessing the current state is start where you are; removing unnecessary steps is keep it simple and practical.

questions.prompt: Which statement about the relationship between the guiding principles is correct?
choices: They interact with and depend on each other
Only one principle should be used in each situation
They must be applied one at a time in a fixed order
Each principle applies to a single value chain activity
questions.explanation: The guiding principles are interconnected; organizations should consider all of them and how they apply together.

questions.prompt: An organization is unsure which guiding principles apply to a new initiative. What does ITIL 4 recommend?
choices: Wait until a problem occurs and then choose the most relevant principle
Consider all of them and judge how relevant each is to the situation
Use only the first principle that seems relevant
Choose the principle that the governing body prefers
questions.explanation: Not every principle is critical in every situation, but all should be reviewed to decide how they apply.

questions.prompt: Which guiding principle reminds teams that they should not try to do everything at once?
choices: Progress iteratively with feedback
Think and work holistically
Focus on value
Collaborate and promote visibility
questions.explanation: Progress iteratively with feedback recommends working in smaller, manageable sections rather than all at once.

questions.prompt: A team uses metrics to show leadership the real benefits achieved by a new self-service portal. Which principle does this BEST support?
choices: Focus on value
Keep it simple and practical
Start where you are
Think and work holistically
questions.explanation: Measuring the benefits delivered to consumers keeps attention on the value the work is meant to create.

questions.prompt: Which guiding principle is MOST concerned with avoiding hidden agendas and building trust across teams?
choices: Collaborate and promote visibility
Start where you are
Focus on value
Keep it simple and practical
questions.explanation: Making work visible and collaborating openly reduces hidden agendas and supports trust and better decisions.

questions.prompt: An organization adopts DevOps tools but leaves team structures, supplier contracts and processes unchanged, and results are poor. Which principle explains why?
choices: Optimize and automate
Start where you are
Think and work holistically
Progress iteratively with feedback
questions.explanation: Changing one element, such as technology, without considering the other dimensions and interactions rarely produces the desired outcomes.

questions.prompt: What is one recommended reason to measure the current state when applying 'start where you are'?
choices: To replace direct observation with automated reports
To prove that the existing process should never change
To provide a baseline for analysing what to keep or change
To allocate blame for poor performance to individuals
questions.explanation: Measurement provides a basis for analysis, though it should be used carefully and complemented by direct observation.

questions.prompt: A team is choosing between several improvement options. Which question MOST reflects 'focus on value'?
choices: Which option best helps our consumers achieve the outcomes they need?
Which option uses the newest technology currently available on the market?
Which option keeps the team's workload unchanged?
Which option was used by the previous manager?
questions.explanation: Focus on value means decisions should be guided by how they create value for stakeholders, especially consumers.

questions.prompt: Which consideration belongs MOST clearly to the organizations and people dimension?
choices: Whether leaders champion values that motivate staff to work well
Whether the workflow from request to delivery has delays
Whether a supplier can provide services at a lower cost
Whether a new tool can integrate with the existing data platforms
questions.explanation: Organizations and people covers culture, leadership, structures, roles and competencies; tools, suppliers and workflows belong to the other dimensions.

questions.prompt: A provider struggles because no one is clear who approves new service designs. Which dimension MOST needs attention?
choices: Value streams and processes
Information and technology
Partners and suppliers
Organizations and people
questions.explanation: Clear roles, responsibilities and systems of authority are part of the organizations and people dimension.

questions.prompt: Which statement about culture in the organizations and people dimension is correct?
choices: Culture is fixed and cannot be influenced by leadership
Culture only matters for staff in customer-facing roles
A culture of trust and transparency supports its objectives
Culture is managed entirely through the partners and suppliers dimension
questions.explanation: ITIL 4 emphasizes a culture that supports objectives, built on trust and transparency and encouraged by leadership.

questions.prompt: Which characteristic of information is MOST relevant when a service desk agent needs current data to resolve an incident?
choices: Ownership
Licensing
Volume
Timeliness
questions.explanation: Information should have qualities such as availability, reliability, accessibility, timeliness, accuracy and relevance for the people who need it.

questions.prompt: A provider is selecting a new platform. Which question is MOST relevant to the information and technology dimension?
choices: Will staff need new competencies and role descriptions?
Will the workflow need new handoffs between teams?
Will the supplier agree to a long-term partnership contract with fixed prices?
Will this technology remain viable and supportable in the foreseeable future?
questions.explanation: The information and technology dimension considers whether technologies are viable, compatible, secure, compliant and supportable.

questions.prompt: A government agency decides not to use public cloud for some data because of strict security rules. Which factor influenced this decision in the information and technology dimension?
choices: The skills profile of the organization's service desk
The organization's strategic focus on core competencies
The nature of its business and the regulations it must follow
The demand patterns of the organization's consumers
questions.explanation: The type of business and the regulations it faces strongly influence the technologies an organization can use.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is MOST likely an emerging technology considered under the information and technology dimension?
choices: Workforce and talent planning
Artificial intelligence and machine learning
Value stream mapping workshops
Supplier performance management
questions.explanation: Information and technology considers technologies such as AI, machine learning, cloud computing and mobile solutions that support services.

questions.prompt: Which consideration is part of the information and technology dimension for a new service?
choices: Which external partner will act as the service integrator for the provider
Which staff will be promoted to lead the service
What information the service will manage and how it will be protected
Which activities make up the delivery workflow
questions.explanation: This dimension covers the information created and managed by services, its security and compliance, and the supporting technology.

questions.prompt: A provider cannot hire specialist database skills quickly enough and engages an external firm. Which factor influencing supplier strategy is this?
choices: External constraints
Demand patterns
Corporate culture
Subject matter expertise
questions.explanation: Organizations may use suppliers when it is more efficient or effective to use a supplier's existing expertise than to develop it internally.

questions.prompt: A company has always preferred to do everything in-house because leadership distrusts outsourcing. Which factor influencing supplier strategy does this show?
choices: Cost concerns
Corporate culture
Subject matter expertise
Resource scarcity
questions.explanation: Some organizations have a historical preference for one approach over another, which is the corporate culture factor.

questions.prompt: A provider uses a supplier for seasonal peaks in call volume rather than hiring permanent staff. Which factor influencing supplier strategy is MOST relevant?
choices: Demand patterns
Strategic focus
External constraints
Corporate culture
questions.explanation: Customer activity and demand may be seasonal or variable, which can influence the use of suppliers for flexible capacity.

questions.prompt: A regulation requires a financial firm to keep certain data processing within its own country, limiting which suppliers it can use. Which factor is this?
choices: Corporate culture
External constraints
Demand patterns
Strategic focus
questions.explanation: Government regulation and other external constraints can restrict or shape an organization's supplier strategy.

questions.prompt: An organization decides to use a supplier because it believes the supplier can deliver more economically than it can itself. Which factor is this?
choices: Subject matter expertise
Resource scarcity
Cost concerns
Corporate culture
questions.explanation: Cost concerns influence supplier strategy when a supplier can provide a service or product more economically.

questions.prompt: Which statement about the partners and suppliers dimension is correct?
choices: It covers contracts and agreements and how services are integrated
It covers only relationships with internal departments and shared services
It applies only to suppliers of hardware and software
It replaces the need for supplier management practices
questions.explanation: The partners and suppliers dimension covers relationships with other organizations, including contracts, agreements and service integration.

questions.prompt: Which question is MOST relevant to the value streams and processes dimension?
choices: Which cloud platform offers the strongest protection for customer data?
Which supplier has the most suitable contract terms?
Which staff members need new competencies?
How do the organization's activities work together to create value?
questions.explanation: Value streams and processes focuses on the activities the organization undertakes, how they are organized, and how they ensure value creation.

questions.prompt: A team removes a redundant approval step that added two days to every order without improving quality. Which dimension is MOST involved?
choices: Information and technology
Organizations and people
Value streams and processes
Partners and suppliers
questions.explanation: Identifying and removing non-value-adding activities from workflows is part of the value streams and processes dimension.

questions.prompt: What does a value stream help an organization identify?
choices: Activities that add value and those that create waste or delay
The staff who should be promoted to management roles
The technologies that are most popular in the market
The suppliers that offer the most profitable contracts for each service
questions.explanation: Mapping a value stream gives a clear picture of the work, helping identify waste and opportunities for improvement.

questions.prompt: Which statement about processes in ITIL 4 is correct?
choices: Processes are the same as organizational structures
Processes define the sequence of actions and their dependencies
Processes are only needed for external customers
Processes describe only the technology used to perform each task
questions.explanation: A process is a set of interrelated activities that transforms inputs into outputs, defining the sequence of actions and their dependencies.

questions.prompt: A provider loses customers because a competitor launches a cheaper, cloud-based alternative. Which PESTLE factor is MOST involved?
choices: Legal
Political
Technological
Environmental
questions.explanation: New technologies that change market options and customer choices are technological external factors, possibly combined with economic ones.

questions.prompt: A change of government leads to new policies on public sector outsourcing that affect a provider's contracts. Which PESTLE factor is this?
choices: Social
Political
Technological
Economic
questions.explanation: Government policy changes are political factors that can constrain or influence how organizations operate.

questions.prompt: Why does ITIL 4 consider external factors when looking at the four dimensions?
choices: External factors only matter during the design of a service
Providers work in dynamic environments that influence them
External factors can be fully controlled by good governance
External factors replace the need to manage the four dimensions
questions.explanation: Factors such as political, economic, social, technological, legal and environmental conditions constrain and influence service providers.

questions.prompt: A provider introduces a new incident tool but staff are not trained and the workflow is unchanged, so the tool is barely used. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: The tool belonged to the wrong PESTLE category
The tool should have been approved by the sponsor
Only one dimension was addressed instead of all four
The tool was implemented before a value stream existed
questions.explanation: Effective services require balanced attention to all four dimensions; technology alone fails without people and process changes.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is part of the organizations and people dimension rather than value streams and processes?
choices: The controls applied at each process step
Staff capacity and competencies to deliver services
The handoffs between teams in a workflow
The order in which activities are performed
questions.explanation: Capacity and competencies of people are part of organizations and people; sequencing, handoffs and controls relate to value streams and processes.

questions.prompt: A provider is concerned that a new service needs to work well with information from several partner systems. Which dimension is MOST involved?
choices: Organizations and people
Value streams and processes
Information and technology
Partners and suppliers
questions.explanation: How information is exchanged between services and systems is a key consideration of the information and technology dimension.

questions.prompt: Which statement about the four dimensions is correct?
choices: They apply to services and to the whole SVS
They are replaced by practices once a service goes live
They apply only to services that use external suppliers
They must be addressed in a strict sequence
questions.explanation: The four dimensions provide a holistic approach and apply both to individual services and to the entire SVS.

questions.prompt: Which statement BEST describes how the service value system converts its inputs into value?
choices: Value is created by suppliers and passed through the SVS unchanged
Practices create value without needing opportunity or demand
Value is created by governance before any demand is received
Opportunity and demand trigger activities in the SVS that create value
questions.explanation: Opportunity and demand are the inputs that trigger SVS activities, which together lead to value creation.

questions.prompt: Why can an organization not always respond to every opportunity or demand?
choices: Opportunities only apply to external consumers
Governance forbids responding to new demand
Demand is always created internally by the provider's own teams
Opportunities and demand can exceed the resources available
questions.explanation: The SVS recognizes that opportunities and demand may not always be acted on immediately; they must be prioritized against available resources.

questions.prompt: Which statement about organizational agility and resilience in the SVS is correct?
choices: Agility is only required during service design
Resilience depends only on the technology used
Agility is achieved by keeping each team strictly separated from others
An integrated SVS helps the organization respond and adapt to change
questions.explanation: The SVS supports flexibility and integration, which help organizations remain agile and resilient as conditions change.

questions.prompt: In the SVS, who is responsible for evaluating, directing and monitoring the organization?
choices: The service owner
The change authority
The service desk
The governing body
questions.explanation: Governance is carried out by the governing body, which evaluates, directs and monitors the organization.

questions.prompt: A board reviews whether current strategies still fit the organization's environment. Which governance activity is this?
choices: Evaluate
Engage
Monitor
Direct
questions.explanation: Evaluate involves examining the organization, its strategy, portfolios and relationships with other parties as circumstances change.

questions.prompt: A governing body assigns responsibility for preparing and implementing a new policy. Which governance activity is this?
choices: Direct
Evaluate
Monitor
Plan
questions.explanation: Direct involves assigning responsibility for, and directing the preparation and implementation of, strategy and policies.

questions.prompt: A governing body checks whether performance and compliance meet the strategy it set. Which governance activity is this?
choices: Evaluate
Direct
Improve
Monitor
questions.explanation: Monitor involves overseeing the performance of the organization and its practices against strategy and policies.

questions.prompt: Which statement about the relationship between governance and continual improvement is correct?
choices: Continual improvement applies to governance too
Continual improvement replaces the need for governance
Governance performs all continual improvement activities
Governance is excluded from continual improvement
questions.explanation: Continual improvement is a recurring organizational activity applied at all levels, including governance.

questions.prompt: How do the activities of the service value chain relate to each other?
choices: They form a separate chain of activities for each practice
They must always be performed in the same linear order
They are used only when developing new services
They are interconnected and exchange inputs and outputs
questions.explanation: Value chain activities are interconnected, each receiving and providing triggers and inputs; they are not a fixed linear sequence.

questions.prompt: Which value chain activity represents the main interaction with stakeholders outside the provider, such as customers and suppliers?
choices: Engage
Deliver and support
Plan
Design and transition
questions.explanation: Engage provides understanding of stakeholder needs and handles the interaction with all stakeholders, including consumers and suppliers.

questions.prompt: A team creates service designs and moves new services into live operation. Which value chain activity is this?
choices: Design and transition
Deliver and support
Obtain/build
Plan
questions.explanation: Design and transition ensures products and services meet stakeholder expectations for quality, costs and time to market, including transitioning them.

questions.prompt: Which value chain activity would typically receive incident and performance information from deliver and support to drive improvement initiatives?
choices: Plan
Engage
Obtain/build
Improve
questions.explanation: Improve receives performance information and improvement opportunities from all value chain activities, including deliver and support.

questions.prompt: Which value chain activity is MOST responsible for ensuring service components meet agreed specifications and are available when needed?
choices: Deliver and support
Engage
Obtain/build
Design and transition
questions.explanation: Obtain/build ensures that service components are available when and where needed and meet agreed specifications.

questions.prompt: An organization defines its future service portfolio, architecture direction and improvement priorities. Which value chain activity is this?
choices: Plan
Design and transition
Engage
Improve
questions.explanation: Plan creates a shared understanding of vision, current status and improvement direction across all dimensions and services.

questions.prompt: Where does demand for a new service, raised by a customer, typically enter the service value chain?
choices: Through governance
Through the engage activity
Through the improve activity
Through the obtain/build activity
questions.explanation: Demand from consumers enters the value chain through engage, where requirements are captured and turned into work.

questions.prompt: Which statement about value streams is correct?
choices: Value streams can only include a single practice
Each organization should define only one value stream for all its work
Value streams replace the service value chain
An organization can define many value streams for different scenarios
questions.explanation: Value streams are combinations of value chain activities and practices; different streams are designed for different scenarios.

questions.prompt: A user reports that an application is not working, and the service is restored. Which value chain activity is MOST central to this value stream?
choices: Obtain/build
Plan
Design and transition
Deliver and support
questions.explanation: Restoring a live service is primarily a deliver and support activity, typically triggered through engage.

questions.prompt: A provider develops a brand-new service requested by a business unit. Which value chain activities are MOST likely to be involved?
choices: Engage and deliver and support only, as with incident handling
Obtain/build only, because the service has to be developed
Engage, design and transition, obtain/build, and deliver and support
Plan and improve only, since new services are strategic
questions.explanation: Developing a new service typically requires most value chain activities, from capturing needs to building, transitioning and supporting it.

questions.prompt: Which statement about practices and the service value chain is correct?
choices: Practices are used only in the deliver and support activity
Each practice belongs to exactly one value chain activity in ITIL 4
Practices are part of governance rather than the value chain
A single practice can contribute to several value chain activities
questions.explanation: Practices are flexible resources that can be used across multiple value chain activities, as needed by each value stream.

questions.prompt: Which component of the SVS ensures that the organization's activities are aligned with policies and strategy?
choices: Governance
Guiding principles
Value streams
Practices
questions.explanation: Governance directs and controls the organization and checks that it remains aligned with strategy and policies.

questions.prompt: Which statement about the guiding principles within the SVS is correct?
choices: They are binding rules that must not be adapted
They are replaced by practices during operations
They are universal and apply to any type of work
They apply only to the plan activity
questions.explanation: The guiding principles are universal and enduring recommendations that can guide decisions in all circumstances.

questions.prompt: In the continual improvement model, a team reviews the organization's mission and goals to understand where an improvement fits. Which step is this?
choices: Where do we want to be?
How do we get there?
What is the vision?
Where are we now?
questions.explanation: The first step links the improvement initiative to the organization's vision and objectives.

questions.prompt: A team collects current performance data before setting improvement targets. Which step of the continual improvement model is this?
choices: What is the vision?
Did we get there?
Where are we now?
Take action
questions.explanation: Where are we now? involves a baseline assessment of the current state, including services, users, culture, processes and technology.

questions.prompt: After a gap analysis, a team sets key performance indicators and target values for an improvement. Which step is this?
choices: Where do we want to be?
Did we get there?
Where are we now?
How do we get there?
questions.explanation: Where do we want to be? defines the target state with measurable objectives, CSFs and KPIs based on the gap between vision and current state.

questions.prompt: During the 'take action' step, what should a team continue to do while executing the plan?
choices: Redefine the vision before each task
Avoid any feedback until the plan is fully completed
Measure progress and adjust the approach as needed
Repeat the baseline assessment every day
questions.explanation: Take action executes the plan, often iteratively, while monitoring progress and managing risks.

questions.prompt: An improvement has met its targets. The team now reinforces new behaviours and communicates the success. Which step of the continual improvement model is this?
choices: How do we keep the momentum going?
Take action
Did we get there?
What is the vision?
questions.explanation: Keeping momentum involves reinforcing the improvement, communicating success and embedding the changes.

questions.prompt: If an improvement does NOT achieve its expected results, what does the continual improvement model suggest?
choices: Stop using the continual improvement model for this work
Analyse why and plan further actions, possibly repeating steps
Immediately reverse all changes made during the improvement
Declare the improvement a success and close it anyway
questions.explanation: If results fall short, the team analyses the reasons and may revisit earlier steps or plan further iterations.

questions.prompt: Which statement about the continual improvement model's steps is correct?
choices: They apply only to large organizational changes
They must always be completed in strict order and never repeated
They can be applied iteratively, not strictly in sequence
They can only be used by a dedicated improvement team
questions.explanation: The model is a guide that can be applied flexibly and iteratively, and at any scale.

questions.prompt: Which statement about the SVS and silos is correct?
choices: Silos are removed automatically when practices are defined
Silos reduce agility; the SVS promotes integration
Silos only exist in organizations without governance
Silos improve control and should be encouraged by the SVS
questions.explanation: Silos can limit communication, collaboration and agility; the SVS promotes integrated and coordinated working.

questions.prompt: What does ITIL 4 describe as the main output of the improve value chain activity?
choices: Improvement initiatives and improvement status reports
Contracts and agreements with external and internal suppliers
Completed service requests and user support tasks
Service components ready for use in live operational environments
questions.explanation: Improve produces improvement initiatives, plans and status reports that are used across the value chain.

questions.prompt: Which value chain activity would typically produce contracts and agreements with external suppliers?
choices: Improve
Deliver and support
Plan
Engage
questions.explanation: Engage interacts with suppliers and partners, producing outputs such as contracts and agreements with external and internal suppliers.

questions.prompt: Which statement about the SVS's inputs is correct?
choices: Opportunity is created only by the governing body of the organization
Demand can come from both internal and external consumers
Only demand, not opportunity, triggers the SVS
Demand comes only from external paying customers
questions.explanation: Demand is the need or desire for products and services among internal and external consumers; opportunity is another SVS input.

questions.prompt: An organization wants continual improvement to be part of everyday work rather than a one-off project. What is the BEST approach?
choices: Assign all improvement work to an external consultancy
Encourage improvement everywhere and secure time and budget
Limit improvement ideas to the IT management team
Run a single improvement programme every five years
questions.explanation: Continual improvement activities include encouraging improvement throughout the organization and securing time and budget for it.

questions.prompt: A small team is set up to lead continual improvement. Which statement about its role is correct?
choices: It only reviews improvements proposed by suppliers
It coordinates improvement, but everyone stays responsible
It becomes solely responsible for every improvement
It replaces the need for a continual improvement register
questions.explanation: A dedicated team may lead and coordinate improvement, but continual improvement is everyone's responsibility.

questions.prompt: Which technique is commonly used in continual improvement to identify strengths, weaknesses, opportunities and threats?
choices: Swarming
SWOT analysis
Value stream deployment
Trend analysis of incidents
questions.explanation: SWOT analysis is one of several techniques, alongside balanced scorecard reviews and maturity assessments, used to support continual improvement.

questions.prompt: A proposed improvement is expensive. What should usually be prepared before it is approved?
choices: A standard change model for the improvement
A major incident procedure for the improvement
A business case justifying the expected value
A new service level agreement for the improvement
questions.explanation: Continual improvement activities include making business cases for improvement actions where appropriate.

questions.prompt: After an improvement is implemented, what should the continual improvement practice do next?
choices: Measure and evaluate the results against the expected outcomes
Close the record without further review
Raise a problem record to investigate the improvement
Ask the service desk to promote the improvement to users
questions.explanation: Measuring and evaluating improvement results is a key continual improvement activity and confirms whether value was achieved.

questions.prompt: Why does ITIL 4 recommend that organizations have staff with deep knowledge of a few improvement methods?
choices: So external suppliers are not needed for any improvement
So the improvement register can be removed
So that only one method is ever used in the organization
So improvement work is applied consistently and effectively
questions.explanation: Some staff should understand key methods and techniques well, so improvement can be applied consistently; many methods can be used.

questions.prompt: A team wants to update a production web server configuration. It is not on the list of standard changes. What should happen FIRST?
choices: Ask the release manager to make the update available to users
Raise a change request for assessment as a normal change
Apply the update and record it as a standard change afterwards
Log an incident so the service desk can approve the update
questions.explanation: Changes that are not pre-authorized standard changes and are not emergencies are handled as normal changes, which need assessment and authorization.

questions.prompt: Which statement about the change authority for normal changes is correct?
choices: It can vary depending on the type and risk of the change
It is always a single change advisory board for the organization
It is always the requester's line manager
It is never required for low-risk changes
questions.explanation: The appropriate change authority depends on the type of change; low-risk changes may be authorized locally, high-risk ones at a higher level.

questions.prompt: In an organization with a highly automated deployment pipeline, how might low-risk normal changes be authorized?
choices: By the service desk after each deployment
Through automated checks built into the pipeline
By converting them all into emergency changes
By the governing body at its quarterly meeting
questions.explanation: In organizations with mature automation, authorization of many normal changes can be automated as part of the pipeline.

questions.prompt: A change request is raised to replace a failed router that is causing a major outage. Which change type is MOST appropriate?
choices: Standard change
Normal change
Emergency change
Service request
questions.explanation: Changes that must be implemented as soon as possible, for example to resolve a major incident, are emergency changes.

questions.prompt: How should emergency changes be tested, according to ITIL 4?
choices: Not at all, because there is never enough time
Only after the next major release has been deployed
As far as practical, even if testing is reduced
Testing is skipped because the change authority's approval replaces it
questions.explanation: Emergency changes are expedited and may have reduced testing because of time constraints, but they should still be assessed and tested as far as is practical before implementation; approval does not replace testing.

questions.prompt: Which statement about the scope of change enablement is correct?
choices: It includes only changes requested by customers or their sponsors
Each organization defines what is in scope for change enablement
It covers only changes to physical hardware
It is fixed by ITIL and cannot be adjusted
questions.explanation: Organizations define the scope of change enablement; typically it covers changes to IT infrastructure, applications, documentation, processes, supplier relationships and more.

questions.prompt: How does change enablement differ from organizational change management?
choices: They are identical practices described with different names
It manages changes to services, not the people side of change
It manages staff restructuring and communication about change
It only manages changes to the organization's business strategy
