questions.explanation: Change enablement focuses on changes to products and services; organizational change management deals with the people aspects of change.

questions.prompt: A team realises its standard password reset change is now causing occasional failures. What is the BEST action?
choices: Review and update the standard change and its risk assessment
Stop recording password resets altogether
Continue using it, since standard changes never need review
Convert all future resets into emergency changes
questions.explanation: Standard changes are pre-authorized based on an initial risk assessment; if circumstances change, the procedure should be reviewed.

questions.prompt: Two teams plan changes to the same system on the same weekend without knowing about each other. Which tool would BEST have prevented this conflict?
choices: The continual improvement register
The service catalogue
The known error database
The change schedule
questions.explanation: The change schedule helps plan changes, communicate them and avoid conflicts between changes.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is MOST likely to be handled as a standard change?
choices: Restoring a failed database after a major outage
Adding a user to an application using a documented procedure
Redesigning the network architecture of a data centre
Migrating all customer data to a new cloud provider
questions.explanation: Standard changes are low-risk, relatively common and follow a documented, pre-authorized procedure.

questions.prompt: An online banking service is down for all customers. How should this incident be prioritized?
choices: As low priority until a problem record is created
As high priority because of its wide impact and urgency
As a service request because many users are affected
In order of arrival with all other incidents
questions.explanation: Incidents are prioritized by impact and urgency, so that incidents with the highest business impact are resolved first.

questions.prompt: According to ITIL 4, by whom may incidents be resolved?
choices: By the service desk, support teams, suppliers or users
Only by specialists once the root cause is known
Only by problem management after escalation
Only by the service desk, as the single point of contact
questions.explanation: ITIL 4 recognizes many resolution routes, including self-help, the service desk, support teams, suppliers and swarming.

questions.prompt: What should the incident management practice do to help users while an incident is being worked on?
choices: Avoid contact until the incident is closed to save agent time
Transfer the user to problem management
Ask the user to raise a change request
Provide good-quality updates and set realistic expectations
questions.explanation: Effective incident management includes timely communication with affected users and setting expectations about progress and resolution.

questions.prompt: A rare incident affects an entire data centre. Which resource is MOST likely needed in addition to normal incident procedures?
choices: The continual improvement register
The standard change catalogue
Disaster recovery plans
The service request catalogue
questions.explanation: Extreme incidents may require invoking disaster recovery plans, which are covered by service continuity management.

questions.prompt: Why should incident records include information about symptoms, business impact and actions taken?
choices: So the incident can be billed to the customer
So the user can be identified for disciplinary action
So it can be managed and the data reused for diagnosis
So the incident can be automatically closed
questions.explanation: Good incident records support effective management, diagnosis, reuse of knowledge and later problem analysis.

questions.prompt: Which practice relationship BEST supports fast incident resolution?
choices: Access to known errors and workarounds from problem management
Access to the change schedule from release management
Access to supplier contracts from relationship management
Access to asset costs from IT asset management
questions.explanation: Known errors and workarounds provide diagnostic information that helps incident management restore service quickly.

questions.prompt: What does ITIL 4 say about the design of incident management processes?
choices: One identical process must be used for all incidents
Different processes may suit different types of incidents
Incident processes must be fully manual to allow judgement
Incident processes are designed by suppliers only
questions.explanation: Organizations may design separate processes for major incidents, security incidents and other types, as appropriate.

questions.prompt: A complex incident has been passed between four support teams, each assuming another owns it. Which approach could resolve this faster?
choices: Raising an emergency change to reassign the incident
Swarming, with the relevant experts working on it together
Logging a service request for further investigation
Closing the incident and opening a new one with a clearer description
questions.explanation: Swarming involves many stakeholders working together on an incident until it is clear who is best placed to continue.

questions.prompt: A user reports that the expense app runs very slowly. Is this an incident?
choices: Yes, because reduced service quality is an incident
No, because the service is still available to the user
No, because slowness is always handled as a service request
Yes, but only if the user cannot log in to the app at all
questions.explanation: An incident is an unplanned interruption or a reduction in the quality of a service, so significant slowness counts.

questions.prompt: Which approach can help users resolve simple incidents without contacting the service desk?
choices: Direct access to the configuration management database and tools
Emergency changes requested directly by users
Escalation of every issue to the supplier
Self-help resources such as knowledge articles and automated tools
questions.explanation: Self-help through portals and knowledge articles allows users to resolve common incidents themselves, and these should still be recorded.

questions.prompt: A service desk notices the same printer error reported 30 times this month. Which practice should investigate the underlying cause?
choices: Release management
Problem management
Service request management
Incident management
questions.explanation: Recurring incidents indicate a problem; problem management identifies and manages the underlying cause.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a source for problem identification?
choices: Information from suppliers and partners about known issues
The continual improvement register and its prioritized ideas
Approved standard change procedures
Completed service request records only
questions.explanation: Problems can be identified from trend analysis, recurring incidents, major incidents, and information from suppliers, partners, developers and testers.

questions.prompt: During a major incident, a team spots a likely underlying cause. What should happen?
choices: A problem may be identified for later investigation
The cause should be ignored until the incident is closed
The incident must be paused until the problem is solved
An emergency change must be raised immediately
questions.explanation: Problem identification can occur during major incident handling; investigation of the cause is then managed through problem management.

questions.prompt: Why does ITIL 4 say that problem analysis should take a holistic view?
choices: Problems are always caused by technology failures
Problems are only relevant to the service desk
Problems must be solved by a single specialist team
Causes may lie in any of the four dimensions
questions.explanation: Causes may lie in people, information and technology, partners and suppliers, or value streams and processes.

questions.prompt: A workaround has been documented for a known error. What does error control do with it over time?
choices: Sends it to the sponsor for budget approval
Reassesses its effectiveness and looks for better solutions
Deletes it once the incident is closed
Converts it into a standard change automatically after review
questions.explanation: Error control regularly reassesses known errors and the effectiveness of workarounds, and identifies potential permanent solutions.

questions.prompt: Problem management identifies a permanent fix that needs a configuration change to a live server. What is the NEXT step?
choices: Apply the fix immediately without authorization
Raise a change request to be assessed and authorized
Close the problem and wait for the next failure
Log a new incident to track the fix
questions.explanation: Problem management may result in a change request; implementing the fix is handled by change enablement.

questions.prompt: Which statement about the interaction between problem management and continual improvement is correct?
choices: They have no relationship in ITIL 4
Continual improvement handles all known errors
Problem management replaces the need for continual improvement
Problem management outcomes can feed improvement opportunities
questions.explanation: Problem management activities can identify improvement opportunities, and solutions may be recorded in the continual improvement register.

questions.prompt: A problem has a low likelihood of recurring and minimal impact. How is it likely to be treated?
choices: With the highest priority, to clear the problem backlog quickly
As an emergency change to remove the risk
As a service request for the service desk
With lower priority than problems posing greater risk
questions.explanation: Problems are prioritized for analysis based on the risk they pose, considering both probability and impact.

questions.prompt: Which skill set is especially important for problem management?
choices: Analytical skills and understanding of complex systems
Contract negotiation and supplier management skills
Marketing and stakeholder communication skills
Customer service and call handling skills
questions.explanation: Problem management requires understanding complex systems and analysing how failures might occur, often across many teams.

questions.prompt: Which statement BEST describes service requests in ITIL 4?
choices: They always require a change request to fulfil
They always indicate that a service has failed
They are only raised by customers, never by users
They are a normal part of delivery, not a failure
questions.explanation: Service requests are pre-defined, user-initiated requests that are part of normal service delivery.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is MOST likely a service request rather than an incident?
choices: A request for a new monitor for a new employee
A laptop that will not start in the morning
An email service that is not receiving messages
A website that shows errors for all users
questions.explanation: Requesting provision of a resource is a service request; failures and degradations are incidents.

questions.prompt: Some service requests are complex and need workflows involving several teams. How should these be handled?
choices: Always as emergency changes
Using standard workflows with defined steps and approvals
Using ad hoc handling each time they occur
By rejecting them until they are simplified
questions.explanation: Service request management uses standardized workflows wherever possible, even for complex requests.

questions.prompt: Which statement about fulfilment of service requests is correct?
choices: Fulfilment times should be set separately for each request
Users should not be told how long fulfilment will take
Users should be told what to expect and when
Users should always contact the supplier directly
questions.explanation: Setting clear expectations about fulfilment times and steps improves user experience and satisfaction.

questions.prompt: A new type of service request is frequently raised but has no defined workflow. What should be done?
choices: Handle it as an incident until users stop raising it
Treat each request as a normal change
Define a standard procedure for handling it
Escalate each request to problem management
questions.explanation: Requests should be predefined and handled through standardized procedures; new common requests should get their own workflow.

questions.prompt: Which service request type covers a user asking to borrow a projector for a meeting?
choices: Feedback, compliments and complaints
Request for access to a resource
Provision of a resource or service
Request for information
questions.explanation: Provision of resources or services, such as equipment, is a common type of service request.

questions.prompt: A user complains that the support team was rude. Which practice should handle this, according to ITIL 4?
choices: Incident management
Service request management
Problem management
Change enablement
questions.explanation: Feedback, compliments and complaints are a type of service request in ITIL 4.

questions.prompt: Which approach does ITIL 4 recommend to improve service request fulfilment over time?
choices: Reduce the number of request types users can raise
Move all requests to the problem management team
Add approval steps to every request to reduce risk
Automate and continually improve fulfilment
questions.explanation: Service request management benefits from automation and continual improvement to increase efficiency and user satisfaction.

questions.prompt: A provider deploys a chatbot that answers common questions before passing users to agents. Which practice is this MOST likely supporting?
choices: Service desk
Change enablement
Supplier management
Problem management
questions.explanation: Service desks increasingly use automation and AI-based tools, such as chatbots, to handle demand and support users.

questions.prompt: Which statement about the service desk's role in the organization is correct?
choices: It is only responsible for logging incidents, not service requests
It is the team that fixes every incident permanently
It should focus only on technical issues and avoid business matters
It strongly influences user experience and perception
questions.explanation: The service desk is the single point of contact and strongly influences user experience and perception of the provider.

questions.prompt: Does a service desk need to be highly technical according to ITIL 4?
choices: No, because the service desk only routes calls to suppliers
Not necessarily; understanding users and the business matters
Yes, every agent must be a technical expert in all services
Yes, because the service desk resolves all problems
questions.explanation: ITIL 4 notes that service desks may be more or less technical, but they must understand users, business processes and the wider organization.

questions.prompt: A user cannot describe their issue clearly and is frustrated. Which service desk skill is MOST important here?
choices: Empathy and effective communication
Advanced programming knowledge
Financial analysis
Contract negotiation
questions.explanation: Service desk staff need soft skills such as empathy, communication and emotional intelligence to support users effectively.

questions.prompt: Which channel would a service desk use to let users log and track requests themselves?
choices: A continual improvement register
A service portal
A change advisory board
A configuration management database
questions.explanation: Service portals are one of the service desk's channels, enabling users to log, track and update their requests and incidents.

questions.prompt: Which statement about the service desk and incident ownership is correct?
choices: It must resolve every incident itself without escalation
It cannot be involved after an incident is logged
It only handles problems, never incidents
It may escalate incidents to support teams to resolve
questions.explanation: The service desk captures demand and may resolve incidents itself or route them to support and development teams.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a benefit of a virtual service desk?
choices: All staff must be located in a single building
It removes the need to provide a single point of contact
Staff in different locations can work together as one desk
It eliminates the need for any support tools
questions.explanation: A virtual service desk lets staff in multiple locations work as one team using shared technology.

questions.prompt: A service desk agent records an incident and provides a workaround from the knowledge base on the first call. Which practice is MOST directly being performed?
choices: Release management, working with deployment management
Service level management, working with supplier management
Service desk, working with incident management
Problem management, working with change enablement
questions.explanation: The service desk captures demand and can resolve incidents at first contact using knowledge and workarounds, as part of incident management.

questions.prompt: Why should service level targets be agreed with customers rather than set solely by IT?
choices: So they reflect what the business values
So suppliers can set their own penalty clauses
So IT can choose targets that are easy to meet
So the service desk can ignore user feedback
questions.explanation: Service level management sets clear business-based targets that reflect what customers actually need and value.

questions.prompt: An SLA measures only system uptime, but users care about completing orders quickly. What is the BEST improvement?
choices: Stop reporting to the customer until uptime improves
Remove all metrics and rely on customer comments
Increase the uptime target to 100 percent
Add metrics linked to the outcomes users care about
questions.explanation: SLAs should relate to defined outcomes, not just operational metrics, to avoid the watermelon effect.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a key requirement for a successful SLA, according to ITIL 4?
choices: It must be agreed only by the service provider
It must be renewed every month without review
It must contain as many technical metrics as possible
It must be simply written and easy to understand
questions.explanation: SLAs should be simply written, easy to understand and use, and agreed by all parties.

questions.prompt: Which activity BEST helps service level management understand customer satisfaction?
choices: Reviewing supplier invoices
Checking the change schedule
Running customer surveys
Analysing configuration item counts
questions.explanation: Customer feedback, through surveys and key business-related measures, is an important input to service level management.

questions.prompt: A customer says SLA reports are full of technical figures they cannot interpret. What should service level management do?
choices: Stop sending the reports altogether
Ask the customer to learn the technical terms
Report service levels in business terms
Add more technical figures to show detail
questions.explanation: Service level reporting should reflect the customer's perspective and business outcomes.

questions.prompt: Which statement about service level management and external suppliers is correct?
choices: Suppliers set the SLAs for the provider's customers
Supplier targets replace the need for customer SLAs
Service level management never involves supplier agreements
Commercial and supplier management skills can be useful
questions.explanation: Service level management involves relationship, business liaison, business analysis and commercial and supplier management skills.

questions.prompt: Which type of metric is MOST useful when combined with operational metrics in service level management?
choices: Metrics on the number of changes raised each month
Business metrics on how services support the business
Metrics on the age of IT equipment only
Metrics on the number of staff in each support team
questions.explanation: Service level management uses operational metrics and business metrics that reflect the service's contribution to business outcomes.

questions.prompt: During a service review, a customer reveals new business priorities. What should service level management do?
choices: Record it as an incident for the service desk
Ignore it until the SLA expires
Use it to update service level targets
Raise a problem to investigate the customer
questions.explanation: Ongoing engagement with customers allows service level management to keep targets aligned with changing needs.

questions.prompt: Which set of concepts is MOST associated with the information security management practice?
choices: Utility, warranty and value
Confidentiality, integrity and availability
Plan, build and deliver
Impact, urgency and priority
questions.explanation: Information security management protects information by managing risks to its confidentiality, integrity and availability.

questions.prompt: Which statement about the information security management practice is correct?
choices: It focuses only on preventing security incidents
It is the sole responsibility of the IT security team
It only applies to externally facing services
It balances prevention, detection and correction
questions.explanation: Information security management must balance prevention, detection and correction, and involves everyone in the organization.

questions.prompt: A provider wants to ensure that users cannot later deny having performed an action in a system. Which aspect of information security does this support?
choices: Capacity
Utility
Availability
Non-repudiation
questions.explanation: Besides confidentiality, integrity and availability, information security also considers aspects such as authentication and non-repudiation.

questions.prompt: A provider wants to understand its key stakeholders' priorities and maintain good links with them at a strategic level. Which practice is MOST relevant?
choices: Service request management
Monitoring and event management
Deployment management
Relationship management
questions.explanation: Relationship management establishes and nurtures links with stakeholders at strategic and tactical levels.

questions.prompt: Which activity is part of the relationship management practice?
choices: Restoring services after stakeholder incidents
Recording configuration items owned by stakeholders
Authorizing changes requested by key stakeholders and sponsors
Identifying, analysing and improving stakeholder relationships
questions.explanation: Relationship management includes identifying, analysing, monitoring and continually improving relationships with and between stakeholders.

questions.prompt: Which activity is part of the supplier management practice?
choices: Negotiating contracts and monitoring supplier performance
Resolving supplier incidents through swarming
Deploying supplier software to live environments
Recording supplier improvement ideas in the change schedule
questions.explanation: Supplier management includes creating a supplier strategy, contract negotiation, relationship management and performance management.

questions.prompt: An organization relies on one strategic partner for all its network services under a close, long-term relationship. Which sourcing approach is this?
choices: Single source or partnership
Insourcing
Multi-sourcing
Emergency sourcing
questions.explanation: Single sourcing or partnership involves one supplier with a close, often strategic, relationship; multi-sourcing spreads services across several.

questions.prompt: Why does supplier management seek to create a single point of visibility and control?
choices: To allow each team to manage suppliers independently
To replace service level management
To remove the need for supplier contracts
To ensure consistency across all suppliers
questions.explanation: Supplier management aims to create a single point of visibility and control over suppliers to ensure consistency.

questions.prompt: An organization finds it is paying for 500 software licences but only 300 are installed. Which practice should address this?
choices: Service desk
Release management
IT asset management
Incident management
questions.explanation: IT asset management controls costs and manages the lifecycle of assets, including software licences.

questions.prompt: Which activity is commonly part of IT asset management?
choices: Defining business-based service level targets
Making new features available to users
Restoring services after unplanned interruptions
Maintaining an asset register and auditing assets
questions.explanation: IT asset management maintains information about assets, often in a register, and uses audits to keep it accurate.

questions.prompt: Which statement BEST describes the difference between IT asset management and service configuration management?
choices: Asset management records relationships; configuration management records costs
Asset management covers value and lifecycle; configuration covers relationships
They are the same practice described using two different names
Asset management covers only hardware; configuration covers only software
questions.explanation: IT asset management manages the financial and lifecycle aspects of assets; service configuration management maintains information about CIs and their relationships.

questions.prompt: A disk usage alert reaches 80 percent, below the critical threshold of 95 percent. What type of event is this MOST likely?
choices: An exception event
An informational event
A warning event
A major incident
questions.explanation: Events can be informational, warnings or exceptions; a warning indicates a threshold is approaching that may require action.

questions.prompt: A monitoring tool detects that a critical service has stopped responding. Which type of event is this?
choices: An exception event that may lead to an incident
A warning event that can be ignored
A standard change that has been completed
An informational event that needs no action
questions.explanation: Exception events indicate something abnormal, such as a service failure, and often lead to incidents being created.

questions.prompt: Which statement about the monitoring and event management practice is correct?
choices: It records only events that cause outages
It replaces the need for incident management
It only collects information about user complaints
It identifies and prioritizes significant events
questions.explanation: Monitoring and event management observes services and components, recording and reporting significant events and establishing appropriate responses.

questions.prompt: Which statement about release management in ITIL 4 is correct?
choices: Release management deploys hardware to data centres
Releases can be made available independently of when they are deployed
Releases must always be made available at the moment of deployment
Release management authorizes all normal changes
questions.explanation: Release and deployment can be separated, for example by deploying components and releasing them later with feature flags.

questions.prompt: In an Agile or DevOps environment, how are releases often managed?
choices: As emergency changes approved by the board
As rare, large releases planned once per year
As frequent, small and often automated releases
As service requests raised by users
questions.explanation: Modern approaches tend to use frequent, small releases supported by automated pipelines.

questions.prompt: Which statement about configuration information is correct?
choices: It should be stored in a single tool by every organization
It is only needed by the service desk
Its value should justify the cost of maintaining it
All possible data about every component should always be recorded
questions.explanation: Service configuration management should balance the value of configuration information against the cost and effort of maintaining it.

questions.prompt: During an incident, a support analyst wants to see which applications depend on a failed server. Which practice provides this information?
choices: IT asset management
Service configuration management
Supplier management
Service level management
questions.explanation: Service configuration management provides information on CIs and their relationships, supporting impact assessment and diagnosis.

questions.prompt: What is a configuration management system (CMS)?
choices: A team that authorizes changes to configuration items
A list of all services offered to customers
Tools and data used to manage configuration information
A process for deploying software to live environments
questions.explanation: A CMS is a set of tools, data and information used to support service configuration management; it may combine several data sources.

questions.prompt: A new software version is moved to a small part of the production environment at a time over several weeks. Which deployment approach is this?
choices: Phased deployment
Emergency deployment
Big bang deployment
Pull deployment
questions.explanation: Phased deployment moves new or changed components to parts of the environment in stages.

questions.prompt: Users download a new application version from a self-service portal when they choose. Which deployment approach is this?
choices: Continuous delivery
Phased deployment
Big bang deployment
Pull deployment
questions.explanation: In pull deployment, software is made available in a controlled repository and users download it when they choose.

questions.prompt: When an organization provides services, which form of value do its shareholders typically expect?
choices: Financial benefits such as dividends
Employment opportunities and taxes paid locally
Career development, job satisfaction and recognition
Reduced costs and risks in their own daily work as users
questions.explanation: ITIL 4 lists financial benefits such as dividends, and a sense of confidence and predictability, as the value shareholders receive. Career development is value for employees, and taxes and jobs are value for society.

questions.prompt: Which ITIL 4 term is the generic role that includes the more specific roles of customer, user and sponsor?
choices: Service provider
Service consumer
Service integrator
Service owner
questions.explanation: When an organization receives services it acts as a service consumer, and the specific consumer roles are customer, user and sponsor.

questions.prompt: How does ITIL 4 describe a service provider?
choices: The person who authorizes the budget for a service
Any external company that sells technology products
A role an organization performs in a service relationship to provide services
The internal department that owns and operates all of the IT infrastructure
questions.explanation: Being a service provider is a role an organization performs in a service relationship; the same organization can be a consumer in other relationships. Authorizing budget is the sponsor's role.

questions.prompt: A new analytics tool lets the sales team prepare monthly forecasts in half the time they took before. Which aspect of the service does this mainly illustrate?
choices: A cost imposed on the consumer by the service
Warranty, because the service has enough capacity for all users
Warranty, because the service is available when needed
Utility, as it supports the consumer's performance
questions.explanation: Utility is what the service does: it either supports the performance of the consumer or removes constraints. Warranty is about how well it performs, such as availability, capacity, security and continuity.

questions.prompt: A provider's support engineers carry out the password resets and data restores that were agreed in the service offering. Which part of the service relationship do these activities belong to?
choices: Service provision
Service relationship management
Service consumption
Service sponsorship
questions.explanation: Fulfilment of agreed service actions is part of service provision, alongside managing the provider's resources and providing access to them. Requesting those actions is part of service consumption.

questions.prompt: A consumer's staff take delivery of new laptops supplied under a service and start managing them as their own property. Which part of the service relationship does receiving these goods belong to?
choices: Service relationship management
Service consumption
Service integration and management
Service provision
questions.explanation: Service consumption includes managing the consumer's resources, users using the service, and receiving (acquiring) goods. Supplying the goods is part of the provider's service provision.

questions.prompt: How is warranty for a service typically expressed and agreed between a provider and its consumers?
choices: Through the price the consumer pays for the service
Through the maximum number of users who can be registered for the service
Through agreed service levels, such as for availability and capacity
Through the list of features the service offers
questions.explanation: Warranty is the assurance that a service will meet agreed requirements, and it is usually related to service levels aligned with consumers' needs. The list of features describes utility.

questions.prompt: Managers keep making poor decisions because the configuration data they rely on contains many wrong entries. Which characteristic of information is MOST clearly lacking?
choices: Timeliness
Accessibility
Availability
Accuracy
questions.explanation: ITIL 4 highlights information characteristics such as availability, reliability, accessibility, timeliness, accuracy and relevance. Wrong entries are an accuracy problem; out-of-date data would be a timeliness problem.

questions.prompt: Within the value streams and processes dimension, what describes in more detail who is involved in a process and how the work should be done?
choices: Procedures and work instructions
Service level agreements
The organizational chart
Supplier contracts
questions.explanation: A process can be defined in more detail using procedures, which outline who is involved, and work instructions, which describe how to carry out specific tasks.

questions.prompt: During service design, a manager checks that every team member understands how their work contributes to creating value. Which dimension is this MAINLY addressing?
choices: Value streams and processes
Organizations and people
Partners and suppliers
Information and technology
questions.explanation: Making sure everyone understands their contribution to value creation is a key consideration of the organizations and people dimension, together with culture, roles and competencies.

questions.prompt: A provider launches a 24x7 support process, but it fails at night because the outsourced vendor's contract only covers business hours. Which dimension was overlooked?
choices: Value streams and processes
Organizations and people
Partners and suppliers
Information and technology
questions.explanation: The supplier's contract and its integration into the service fall under the partners and suppliers dimension. All four dimensions must be considered when designing a process.

questions.prompt: A provider has a formal contract with clearly separated responsibilities with one supplier, and a flexible partnership with shared goals and risks with another. What does the partners and suppliers dimension say about this?
choices: Partnerships are allowed only with hardware suppliers
Shared risks mean the partner becomes a service consumer
Only formal contracts with fixed penalties are acceptable
Both are valid forms of relationship between organizations
questions.explanation: ITIL 4 describes a range of relationships between organizations, from formal contracts with clear demarcation of responsibilities to flexible partnerships where goals and risks are shared.

questions.prompt: A weekly report given to a manager is full of data that has nothing to do with the decision she must make. Which characteristic of information is MOST clearly lacking?
choices: Relevance
Availability
Timeliness
Accuracy
questions.explanation: Relevance is one of the information characteristics considered in the information and technology dimension; data that does not relate to the decision being made has little value, however accurate or current it is.

questions.prompt: A team spends months analysing every part of a large system before taking any action. Which piece of advice from 'progress iteratively with feedback' applies?
choices: Do fewer things, but do them better
Comprehend the whole, but do something
Decisions can only be made on visible data
Collaboration does not mean consensus
questions.explanation: 'Comprehend the whole, but do something' warns that waiting to understand everything perfectly can stall progress; teams should understand the big picture yet still make progress in iterations.

questions.prompt: A team argues that because iterations are small, they can be delivered half-finished. Which advice from 'progress iteratively with feedback' counters this?
choices: Comprehend the whole, but do something
Simplicity is the ultimate sophistication
Fast does not mean incomplete
Respect the time of the people involved
questions.explanation: 'Fast does not mean incomplete' means that even small iterations should be complete enough to deliver something of value, not partial work.

questions.prompt: A project lead insists that no decision can be made until every stakeholder agrees completely. What does 'collaborate and promote visibility' say about this?
choices: Decisions should be kept private until complete
Every stakeholder must sign off each step
Only senior managers should be consulted
Collaboration does not mean consensus
questions.explanation: ITIL 4 notes that collaboration does not mean consensus; it is not always necessary or appropriate to get everyone's agreement before moving forward.

questions.prompt: Managers cannot decide which improvements to fund because no one can see how work flows or where it is delayed. Which advice from 'collaborate and promote visibility' applies MOST?
choices: Decisions can only be made on visible data
Do fewer things, but do them better
Fast does not mean incomplete
Recognize the complexity of the systems
questions.explanation: Making work, bottlenecks and data visible lets stakeholders make informed decisions. Without visibility, decisions are made on assumptions.

questions.prompt: A team tries to improve a dozen processes at the same time and does none of them well. Which advice from 'keep it simple and practical' fits BEST?
choices: Automate everything that can be automated
Do fewer things, but do them better
Collaboration does not mean consensus
Comprehend the whole, but do something
questions.explanation: 'Do fewer things, but do them better' encourages focusing effort on the most valuable outcomes rather than spreading resources thinly.

questions.prompt: According to 'focus on value', when should an organization apply a focus on value?
choices: Only after a customer complaint is received
Only during annual strategy reviews
In everyday operations as well as in improvement work
Only when a new service is being designed and built
questions.explanation: ITIL 4 advises focusing on value during everyday operational work as well as in every step of improvement initiatives, and encouraging this focus among all staff.

questions.prompt: After assessing its current service desk tools, a team concludes that none of them can be reused. What does 'start where you are' say about this situation?
choices: The team should keep using the old tools indefinitely
The assessment must be repeated until something reusable is found
Something must always be reused, however poor its current quality is
Sometimes nothing can be reused, and that should be accepted
questions.explanation: While 'start where you are' encourages reuse, it also recognizes that sometimes nothing from the current state is suitable and a fresh start is justified.

questions.prompt: When applying 'start where you are' to decide whether existing practices can be replicated or expanded, which skills does ITIL 4 recommend applying?
choices: Risk management skills
Contract negotiation skills
Financial auditing skills
Software development skills
questions.explanation: ITIL 4 advises applying risk management skills when deciding whether to reuse, replicate or expand existing services and practices, since reuse carries its own risks.

questions.prompt: When optimizing a process, which step follows assessing its current state?
choices: Remove stakeholders from the decision so that progress is faster
Agree the future state and priorities, focusing on simplicity and value
Stop measuring the process to avoid introducing measurement bias
Automate every manual task immediately, before any further analysis
questions.explanation: The recommended optimization steps include understanding the context, assessing the current state, agreeing the future state and priorities with a focus on simplicity and value, engaging stakeholders, executing iteratively and monitoring continually.

questions.prompt: A team applying 'optimize and automate' asks whether it should consider the other guiding principles as well. What does ITIL 4 advise?
choices: Apply only this principle so the work stays focused
Apply the other principles only to manual tasks
Use the other guiding principles when applying this one
Consider other principles only after automation is complete
questions.explanation: ITIL 4 explicitly advises using the other guiding principles, such as 'keep it simple and practical' and 'focus on value', when optimizing and automating.

questions.prompt: According to 'think and work holistically', how should an organization deal with systems of differing complexity?
choices: Use one fixed decision-making method for every system
Leave complex systems unchanged to avoid risk
Treat every system as simple so that work always stays practical
Use different decision-making approaches for different levels of complexity
questions.explanation: ITIL 4 advises recognizing the complexity of systems, because different levels of complexity require different heuristics for decision-making.

questions.prompt: In which forms does continual improvement appear in ITIL 4?
choices: As an SVS component, a value chain activity, a practice and a model
Only as one of the seven guiding principles that apply to all work
Only as a value chain activity
Only as part of governance
questions.explanation: Continual improvement is an SVS component, appears as the 'improve' value chain activity, is one of the management practices, and is supported by the continual improvement model.

questions.prompt: How does ITIL 4 organize its 34 management practices?
choices: Into strategy, design, transition, operation and improvement practices
Into general, service and technical management practices
Into plan, build, run and improve practices
Into people, process, partner and product practices
questions.explanation: ITIL 4 groups its 34 practices into general management practices, service management practices and technical management practices.

questions.prompt: Which group of ITIL 4 management practices includes deployment management?
choices: Service management practices
General management practices
Technical management practices
Governance practices
questions.explanation: Deployment management is one of the three technical management practices, together with infrastructure and platform management and software development and management.

questions.prompt: Which group of ITIL 4 management practices includes information security management?
choices: Value chain practices
Service management practices
Technical management practices
General management practices
questions.explanation: Information security management is a general management practice, as are continual improvement, relationship management and supplier management.

questions.prompt: Which value chain activity passes new and changed products and services to deliver and support?
choices: Design and transition
Plan
Obtain/build
Engage
questions.explanation: Design and transition produces new and changed products and services for deliver and support, along with requirements and specifications for obtain/build.

questions.prompt: Which value chain activity provides consolidated demands and opportunities to the plan activity?
choices: Deliver and support
Engage
Obtain/build
Design and transition
questions.explanation: Engage interacts with stakeholders and passes consolidated demands and opportunities to plan, as well as product and service requirements to design and transition.

questions.prompt: While supporting a live service, the support team identifies that a service component needs to be modified. To which value chain activity does deliver and support send the resulting change request?
choices: Plan
Engage
Obtain/build
Improve
questions.explanation: Outputs of deliver and support include change requests for obtain/build, as well as performance information for engage and improve and improvement opportunities for improve.

questions.prompt: A new automation technology appears that could cut the cost of running several services, although no consumer has asked for it. In SVS terms, what is this?
choices: Demand
A value stream
An output of governance
An opportunity
questions.explanation: Opportunities are options or possibilities to add value or improve the organization. Demand is the need or desire for products and services from consumers.

questions.prompt: A business unit asks the IT department for a new self-service reporting capability. In SVS terms, what does this request represent?
choices: Demand
An opportunity
A guiding principle
A practice
questions.explanation: Demand is the need or desire for products and services among internal and external consumers, and is one of the two inputs to the SVS together with opportunity.

questions.prompt: How does ITIL 4 define a service request?
choices: Any unplanned interruption or quality reduction reported by a user
A user request that initiates an agreed service action
A request to modify a configuration item in production
A complaint raised against a service level target
questions.explanation: A service request initiates a service action that has been agreed as a normal part of service delivery. An unplanned interruption is an incident, and modifying a CI is a change.

questions.prompt: How does ITIL 4 define a service level?
choices: A written contract between a provider and a supplier
The number of users a service can support
Metrics that define expected or achieved service quality
A ranking of services by their business importance and priority
questions.explanation: A service level is one or more metrics that define expected or achieved service quality; service levels are documented in agreements such as SLAs.

questions.prompt: How does ITIL 4 define a release?
choices: The movement of components into a live environment
A request to add or remove a configuration item
An authorization for a normal change
A version of a service or CI made available for use
questions.explanation: A release is a version of a service or CI(s) made available for use. Moving components to live environments is deployment, which can happen separately from release.

questions.prompt: A monitoring tool records that the nightly backup completed successfully. Which type of event is this MOST likely?
choices: An informational event
A major incident
A warning event
An exception event
questions.explanation: Informational events do not require action but may be useful for analysis. Warning events signal that a threshold is being approached, and exception events indicate a breach or failure that needs action.

questions.prompt: An organization moves all users to a new version of an application at the same time in one deployment. Which deployment approach is this?
choices: Pull deployment
Big bang deployment
Continuous delivery
Phased deployment
questions.explanation: In a big bang deployment, new or changed components are deployed to all targets at once. Phased deployment moves them to parts of the environment at a time.

questions.prompt: A team integrates, tests and deploys components whenever they are needed, with frequent feedback loops between development and operations. Which deployment approach is this?
choices: Phased deployment
Big bang deployment
Continuous delivery
Pull deployment
questions.explanation: With continuous delivery, components are integrated, tested and deployed when needed, providing frequent opportunities for customer feedback loops.

questions.prompt: An attack overloads the HR system so that authorized staff cannot use it for several hours, although no data is changed or disclosed. Which aspect of information security is MAINLY affected?
choices: Integrity
Authentication
Confidentiality
Availability
questions.explanation: Availability means information is accessible and usable by authorized people when needed. Integrity concerns unauthorized changes, and confidentiality concerns unauthorized disclosure.

questions.prompt: An organization uses several different suppliers to provide parts of its network, hosting and support services. Which sourcing model is this?
choices: Multi-sourcing
Service integration only
Insourcing
Single source or partnership
questions.explanation: Multi-sourcing means obtaining products and services from more than one supplier. Single sourcing or partnership relies on one strategic supplier.

questions.prompt: An organization decides to use its own internal staff and resources to design, develop and maintain its services rather than using external suppliers. Which sourcing model is this?
choices: Outsourcing
Insourcing
Partnership
Multi-sourcing
questions.explanation: Insourcing is the use of internal resources to design, develop, maintain, run and support products and services. Outsourcing uses external suppliers for these activities.

questions.prompt: A provider uses checksums and access controls to ensure that customer records cannot be altered without authorization. Which aspect of information security does this MAINLY protect?
choices: Availability
Non-repudiation
Integrity
Confidentiality
questions.explanation: Integrity means information is accurate and complete and is protected from unauthorized modification. Confidentiality protects it from unauthorized disclosure.

questions.prompt: A user asks for the toner cartridge in a team printer to be replaced. Which type of service request is this?
choices: Feedback, a compliment or a complaint
A request for information
A request for access to a resource
A request for a service delivery action
questions.explanation: ITIL 4 lists replacing a toner cartridge or providing a report as examples of requests for a service delivery action.

questions.prompt: Shortly after a weekend of changes, users report failures in a business application. How can the change schedule help in this situation?
choices: It shows recent changes, which helps incident and problem management
It is used only to plan future changes, so it cannot help after deployment
It automatically rolls back all recent changes
It replaces the need to raise incident records
questions.explanation: Besides planning and avoiding conflicts, the change schedule provides information after changes are deployed that is useful for incident management, problem management and improvement planning.

questions.prompt: Two business units keep raising conflicting priorities for the IT department's limited resources. Which practice is MOST relevant to understanding their needs and mediating the conflict?
choices: IT asset management
Relationship management
Deployment management
Monitoring and event management
questions.explanation: Relationship management establishes and nurtures links with stakeholders, helping understand their needs and resolve conflicting requirements at strategic and tactical levels.

questions.prompt: How are standard changes, such as installing approved software for a user, often initiated?
choices: As emergency change requests
As problem records
As service requests
Through a full change advisory board review
questions.explanation: Standard changes are low-risk and pre-authorized, so they are commonly initiated as service requests and fulfilled through a defined procedure.

questions.prompt: Which of the following can be treated as a configuration item in service configuration management?
choices: Only software installed in the production environment
Only items that have a financial value recorded on the asset register
Only physical hardware such as servers and network devices
A service, as well as hardware, software and documentation
questions.explanation: Service configuration management manages information about a wide variety of CIs, including hardware, software, networks, buildings, people, suppliers and documentation; services are also treated as CIs.

questions.prompt: An organization wants to make sure old laptops are tracked until they are securely wiped and disposed of, and that reusable parts are recovered. Which practice is MOST relevant?
choices: IT asset management
Release management
Service desk
Service level management
questions.explanation: IT asset management covers the full lifecycle of IT assets, including decisions about reuse and retirement, to maximize value, control costs and manage risks.

questions.prompt: Which practice gives users a clear path to report issues, queries and requests and have them acknowledged, classified, owned and actioned?
choices: Problem management
Service desk
Change enablement
Service configuration management
questions.explanation: The service desk is the single point of contact for users and provides a clear path for reporting issues, queries and requests and having them acknowledged, classified, owned and actioned.

questions.prompt: A company trains its staff and maintains the laptops they need in order to access a provider's cloud CRM platform. In which part of the service relationship does this activity belong?
choices: Service provision
Service relationship management
Service consumption
Service offering design
questions.explanation: Service consumption includes management of the consumer's own resources needed to use the service. Service provision covers the provider's resources and activities.

questions.prompt: A hosting provider continuously monitors the performance of its platform and makes improvements to it. In which part of the service relationship does this activity belong?
choices: Service consumption
Service provision
Service relationship management
Service request management
questions.explanation: Service provision includes service performance management and continual improvement carried out by the provider, along with managing its resources and fulfilling agreed service actions.

questions.prompt: A provider and a consumer hold regular joint reviews to make sure the service, based on the agreed offering, continues to co-create value for both of them. What is this an example of?
choices: Service provision by the provider
Service consumption by the consumer
Service level agreement monitoring
Service relationship management
questions.explanation: Service relationship management is the set of joint activities performed by the provider and consumer to ensure continual value co-creation based on agreed and available service offerings.

questions.prompt: A provider guarantees that, if its primary data centre is lost, the service will be restored from a secondary site within four hours. Which aspect of warranty does this mainly address?
choices: Capacity
Continuity
Utility
Functionality
questions.explanation: Warranty typically covers availability, capacity, security and continuity. A guarantee about recovering after a major disruption is about continuity. Utility and functionality describe what the service does, not how well it is assured.

questions.prompt: Which statement about organizations is correct according to ITIL 4?
choices: It must be a registered legal entity with several employees
It can range from one person to a complex network of entities
It can act only as a provider or only as a consumer at once
It is defined by owning its own technology and its own staff
questions.explanation: ITIL 4 defines an organization as a person or group of people with its own functions, responsibilities, authorities and relationships, varying in size and complexity, and able to act as both provider and consumer.

questions.prompt: Remote working was previously impossible for a firm's staff. A new secure access service now lets them work from home. Which aspect of the service does this mainly describe?
choices: Warranty, because it is secure
Warranty, because it is always available
Utility, because it removes a constraint
Utility, because it lowers the cost
questions.explanation: Utility is the functionality that meets a need, either by supporting the consumer's performance or by removing constraints. Enabling work that was not possible before removes a constraint.

questions.prompt: A service provider donates money and gives staff paid volunteering days to a local charity. According to ITIL 4, what form of value does the charity receive?
choices: Employment and taxes from the provider
Financial and non-financial contributions
Improved image and reputation
Funding paid by service consumers
questions.explanation: ITIL 4 describes value for charity organizations as financial and non-financial contributions from organizations. Employment and taxes are value for society, and image and reputation are value for the provider.

questions.prompt: A provider designs a service on its own and assumes consumers will passively receive whatever value it delivers. Which ITIL 4 concept does this approach contradict?
choices: Service consumption
Utility and warranty
Value co-creation
Service offering
questions.explanation: ITIL 4 states that value is co-created through active collaboration between providers and consumers, not simply delivered by the provider to the consumer.

questions.prompt: According to ITIL 4, between whom are service relationships established?
choices: A provider and its suppliers only
Only a customer and a user within one team
The governing body and the service desk
Two or more organizations, to co-create value
questions.explanation: Service relationships are established between two or more organizations to co-create value, with organizations taking on provider and consumer roles.

questions.prompt: Besides a possible event that could cause harm or loss, how else can risk be defined in ITIL 4?
choices: The total cost of a service that has failed
A known error with no documented workaround
Uncertainty of outcome, positive or negative
The gap between a service's utility and warranty
questions.explanation: ITIL 4 notes that risk can also be defined as uncertainty of outcome, which is used when measuring the probability of both positive and negative outcomes.

questions.prompt: A parent chooses the features of a children's learning app and pays the subscription, but only the child uses it. Which roles does the parent hold?
choices: User and sponsor
Customer and sponsor
Customer and user
Sponsor only
questions.explanation: The parent defines the requirements (customer) and authorizes the budget (sponsor). The child is the user.

questions.prompt: Two companies buy exactly the same service. One considers it highly valuable, while the other sees little benefit. Why is this consistent with ITIL 4?
choices: Value is fixed and set by the provider's price
Value depends only on the warranty offered
Value is perceived differently by each stakeholder
Value is the same for every consumer of a service
questions.explanation: ITIL 4 defines value as the perceived benefits, usefulness and importance of something, so different stakeholders can see different value in the same service.

questions.prompt: Before launch, a provider tests that a new booking site can handle peak holiday traffic and recovers quickly from failures. Which aspect of the service is being confirmed?
choices: Utility
Outcome
Service offering
Warranty
questions.explanation: Warranty is the assurance that a service will meet agreed requirements, such as capacity, availability and continuity. Utility is about what the service does, not how reliably.

questions.prompt: A hospital IT team must choose which of two upgrades to do first. The manager asks which upgrade will do more to help clinicians achieve better patient outcomes. Which guiding principle is the manager applying?
choices: Focus on value
Start where you are
Optimize and automate
Keep it simple and practical
questions.explanation: Focus on value says that everything the organization does should link back to value for its stakeholders, so options are compared by the outcomes they enable.

questions.prompt: Before redesigning a self-service portal, a team watches users carry out common tasks to see where they struggle, instead of relying only on survey results. Which guiding principle does this reflect?
choices: Start where you are
Progress iteratively with feedback
Think and work holistically
Optimize and automate
questions.explanation: Start where you are advises assessing the current state objectively, using direct observation where possible, because reports and measures alone can be misleading.

questions.prompt: A retailer releases a new checkout feature to 5 percent of customers, measures the results and adjusts the design before the next release. Which guiding principle is being applied?
choices: Focus on value
Progress iteratively with feedback
Collaborate and promote visibility
Start where you are
questions.explanation: Delivering in small steps and using feedback from each step to shape the next is the core of progress iteratively with feedback.

questions.prompt: A proposed change to server patching is reviewed for its effect on the service desk, suppliers and security teams, not just the server team. Which guiding principle does this show?
choices: Think and work holistically
Keep it simple and practical
Start where you are
Progress iteratively with feedback
questions.explanation: Think and work holistically recognizes that no service, practice or team stands alone, so changes must consider their effects on the whole system.

questions.prompt: Before automating password resets, a team first removes two unnecessary approval steps from the manual process. Which guiding principle is being followed?
choices: Optimize and automate
Collaborate and promote visibility
Focus on value
Start where you are
questions.explanation: Optimize and automate advises simplifying and optimizing a process before automating it, so that waste is not automated.

questions.prompt: An organization changes its strategy, its type of work and its management structure. How does this affect the ITIL 4 guiding principles?
choices: They still apply; they are universal and enduring
They must be rewritten to match the new strategy
Only the principles linked to strategy still apply
They lapse until a new framework is adopted
questions.explanation: The guiding principles are recommendations that can guide an organization in all circumstances, regardless of changes in its goals, strategies, type of work or management structure.

questions.prompt: Why do the ITIL 4 guiding principles fit well with methods such as Lean, Agile and DevOps?
choices: They were copied directly from the Agile Manifesto
Their messages appear in many other frameworks too
They apply only when those methods are in use
They fully replace the need for those methods
questions.explanation: The guiding principles embody core messages of service management that are also reflected in many other frameworks, methods and standards, which helps organizations combine them.

questions.prompt: An analyst notices that incidents in three different services always follow the same supplier's maintenance window. Which guiding principle encourages looking for patterns like this across system elements?
choices: Focus on value
Keep it simple and practical
Think and work holistically
Optimize and automate
questions.explanation: Think and work holistically advises recognizing the complexity of systems and looking for patterns in the needs of, and interactions between, system elements.

questions.prompt: A request form has 25 fields. The team checks whether each field contributes to a decision or outcome and removes the rest. Which guiding principle is being applied?
choices: Start where you are
Keep it simple and practical
Collaborate and promote visibility
Progress iteratively with feedback
questions.explanation: Keep it simple and practical says to use outcome-based thinking and eliminate anything that does not provide value or produce a useful outcome.

questions.prompt: An IT team presents the benefits of an improvement to finance executives in terms of cost and business risk rather than technical detail. Which guiding principle does this reflect?
choices: Collaborate and promote visibility
Think and work holistically
Optimize and automate
Start where you are
questions.explanation: Collaborate and promote visibility includes communicating in a way the audience can hear, choosing the right message and method for each stakeholder group.

questions.prompt: Users keep abandoning a self-service portal halfway through, so the team redesigns it to be easier to use. Which guiding principle does attention to user experience mainly support?
choices: Focus on value
Start where you are
Optimize and automate
Think and work holistically
questions.explanation: Focus on value includes paying attention to customer experience and user experience, because they strongly affect the value stakeholders perceive.

questions.prompt: After a merger, a team must combine two service desks. It first assesses which of the acquired company's practices already work well and could be kept. Which guiding principle is this?
choices: Start where you are
Keep it simple and practical
Progress iteratively with feedback
Focus on value
questions.explanation: Start where you are advises not starting from scratch, but assessing what already exists and reusing or building on what works.

questions.prompt: When designing a new request form, a team invites end users as well as their managers to the design workshops. Which guiding principle does this reflect?
choices: Optimize and automate
Collaborate and promote visibility
Start where you are
Keep it simple and practical
questions.explanation: Collaborate and promote visibility advises involving the right people in the right roles, including those who will actually use the result, to gain buy-in and better outcomes.

questions.prompt: Why does ITIL 4 warn against relying on technology without the capability for human intervention when applying optimize and automate?
choices: Automated tasks always give less accurate results than people
Human intervention is required by law for all automated tasks
Automation should wait until every process is fully mature
Automating for its own sake can raise costs and cut resilience
questions.explanation: ITIL 4 notes that automation for automation's sake can increase costs and reduce organizational robustness and resilience, so human intervention should remain possible where it adds value.

questions.prompt: According to keep it simple and practical, why should a new procedure be easy to understand?
choices: Simple procedures never need to be reviewed again
Simple procedures remove the need for training records
Easier-to-understand things are more likely to be adopted
Complex procedures cannot be automated at a later stage
questions.explanation: One of the key points of keep it simple and practical is that, to be adopted, things must be easy to understand; simplicity also respects people's time and supports quick wins.

questions.prompt: A provider defines how long ticket data must be kept, how it is archived and how it is securely disposed of. Which dimension of service management does this mainly concern?
choices: Organizations and people
Partners and suppliers
Value streams and processes
Information and technology
questions.explanation: The information and technology dimension includes how information is managed, protected, archived and disposed of, as well as the technologies that support services.

questions.prompt: A provider wants to understand how its different teams work together in an integrated and coordinated way to create value for customers. Which dimension of service management does this concern?
choices: Organizations and people
Value streams and processes
Information and technology
Partners and suppliers
questions.explanation: The value streams and processes dimension defines the activities, workflows, controls and procedures, and how the parts of the organization work together to enable value creation.

questions.prompt: A provider changes its reward scheme so that staff are recognized for helping other teams, not only for closing their own tickets. Which dimension is mainly involved?
choices: Organizations and people
Value streams and processes
Information and technology
Partners and suppliers
questions.explanation: The organizations and people dimension covers culture, roles, staffing, competencies and how staff are motivated and incentivized, which shapes collaborative behaviour.

questions.prompt: A small creative agency rejects a rigid, tightly locked-down tool set because it clashes with the agency's informal and experimental way of working. Which dimension does this consideration belong to?
choices: Partners and suppliers
Value streams and processes
Organizations and people
Information and technology
questions.explanation: Within the information and technology dimension, ITIL 4 notes that an organization's culture and the nature of its business can significantly affect the technologies it chooses.

questions.prompt: A provider reviews its contract with a cloud hosting firm to make sure responsibility for backups is clearly allocated between them. Which dimension is mainly involved?
choices: Information and technology
Organizations and people
Value streams and processes
Partners and suppliers
questions.explanation: The partners and suppliers dimension covers relationships with other organizations involved in delivering services, including contracts, agreements and how responsibilities are divided.

questions.prompt: A new service is launched with excellent technology and processes, but it fails because nobody was given responsibility for supporting it. Which dimension was MOST neglected?
choices: Information and technology
Partners and suppliers
Value streams and processes
Organizations and people
questions.explanation: Clear roles, responsibilities and staffing are part of the organizations and people dimension. All four dimensions must be addressed for a service to deliver value.

questions.prompt: In which group of ITIL 4 management practices is the service desk practice found?
choices: General management practices
Technical management practices
Service management practices
Governance practices
questions.explanation: ITIL 4 groups its 34 practices into general management, service management and technical management practices. The service desk is a service management practice.

questions.prompt: What can serve as an input to a service value chain activity?
choices: External demand or outputs from other activities
Only demand that enters through the engage activity
Only the outputs produced by the plan activity
Only the guiding principles and governance policies
questions.explanation: Each value chain activity transforms inputs into outputs. Inputs can be demand from outside the value chain or outputs of other activities, so activities connect in many different ways.

questions.prompt: A team reaches the take action step of the continual improvement model. Which approach does ITIL 4 say can be used to carry out the plan?
choices: Only Agile, because improvement must always be iterative
Only waterfall, because the plan has already been agreed
Waterfall-style or Agile, whichever suits the plan
No approach, because this step only reviews results
questions.explanation: ITIL 4 notes that the improvement plan could be executed with a traditional waterfall-style approach, but an Agile approach may be more appropriate in many cases.

questions.prompt: Why does the continual improvement model include the step Did we get there?
choices: Executing a plan does not prove the benefits were achieved
Every improvement must be approved by the governing body
The vision must be redefined after every single action
It is the step where the improvement is first funded
questions.explanation: Too often it is assumed that once a plan is acted on, the benefits have been achieved. Did we get there checks the results against the targets that were set.

questions.prompt: What distinguishes the technical management practices from the other ITIL 4 practice groups?
choices: They were adopted from general business management
They were adapted from technology management domains
They were developed entirely within the ITSM industry
They apply only to organizations that write software
questions.explanation: Technical management practices are adapted from technology management domains by shifting their focus from technology solutions to IT services. General management practices come from business management, and service management practices from ITSM.

questions.prompt: According to ITIL 4, to what can the continual improvement model be applied?
choices: The whole SVS and all products, services and relationships
Only to processes in the deliver and support activity
Only to projects approved by the governing body
Only to IT services, not to the wider organization
questions.explanation: The continual improvement model applies to the SVS in its entirety, as well as to all of the organization's products, services, service components and relationships.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is an ITIL 4 technical management practice?
choices: Infrastructure and platform management
Service configuration management
Organizational change management
Relationship management
questions.explanation: The three technical management practices are deployment management, infrastructure and platform management, and software development and management. Relationship management is a general practice; the others are service management practices.

questions.prompt: An organization introduces policies, controls and staff training to prevent, detect and correct breaches of the customer data it relies on. Which practice is MOST involved?
choices: Service configuration management
IT asset management
Monitoring and event management
Information security management
questions.explanation: The purpose of information security management is to protect the information needed by the organization to conduct its business, by managing risks to confidentiality, integrity and availability.

questions.prompt: A provider requires staff to prove who they are with multi-factor authentication before they can open patient records. Which aspect of information security is this mainly addressing?
choices: Integrity
Non-repudiation
Availability
Authentication
questions.explanation: Information security management covers confidentiality, integrity and availability, as well as authentication (verifying identity) and non-repudiation (preventing denial of actions).

questions.prompt: A provider encrypts customer files so that only authorized people can read them, even if the storage is stolen. Which aspect of information security does this mainly protect?
choices: Confidentiality
Availability
Integrity
Non-repudiation
questions.explanation: Confidentiality means information is accessible only to those authorized to see it. Integrity is about preventing unauthorized changes, and availability about access when needed.

questions.prompt: A new marketing director has no working relationship with IT. The provider sets up regular strategic meetings to understand her goals and build trust. Which practice is this MOST associated with?
choices: Service level management
Supplier management
Relationship management
Service desk
questions.explanation: The purpose of relationship management is to establish and nurture the links between the organization and its stakeholders at strategic and tactical levels.

questions.prompt: A company checks its cloud provider's performance against the contract and negotiates improvements where targets are missed. Which practice is MOST involved?
choices: Relationship management
Service level management
Supplier management
Continual improvement
questions.explanation: Supplier management ensures that the organization's suppliers and their performance are managed appropriately to support the seamless provision of quality products and services.

questions.prompt: During a vendor audit, an organization must prove that its installed software matches the licences it has bought. Which practice is MOST responsible for this?
choices: Service configuration management
IT asset management
Release management
Deployment management
questions.explanation: IT asset management plans and manages the full lifecycle of IT assets, which includes helping the organization meet regulatory and contractual requirements such as licence compliance.

questions.prompt: A team sets up tools to continuously observe network devices and to record and report significant changes of state for follow-up. Which practice is this?
choices: Monitoring and event management
Incident management
Service configuration management
Infrastructure and platform management
questions.explanation: Monitoring and event management systematically observes services and service components, and records and reports selected changes of state identified as events.

questions.prompt: A provider bundles several changes into a new version and decides when customers will get access to it, with release notes and user training. Which practice is MOST involved?
choices: Deployment management
Change enablement
Service request management
Release management
questions.explanation: The purpose of release management is to make new and changed services and features available for use. Deployment management moves components to environments, which may happen separately.

questions.prompt: While assessing a planned database upgrade, the change team needs to know which services depend on that database. Which practice provides this information?
choices: IT asset management
Monitoring and event management
Service configuration management
Relationship management
questions.explanation: Service configuration management ensures accurate and reliable information about the configuration of services and the CIs that support them, including their relationships, is available when needed.

questions.prompt: A team moves a new software build into the test environment, then into staging, and finally into production. Which practice is responsible for moving these components between environments?
choices: Release management
Change enablement
Service validation and testing
Deployment management
questions.explanation: Deployment management moves new or changed components to live environments and may also be involved in deploying them to other environments for testing or staging.

questions.prompt: An organization transfers all of its payroll processing to an external company, which then runs it on the organization's behalf. Which sourcing approach is this?
choices: Insourcing
Multi-sourcing
Outsourcing
Service integration and management
