questions.explanation: Outsourcing means using one or more external suppliers to provide products and services that were previously provided internally. Insourcing keeps the work in-house.

questions.prompt: Teams submit many good improvement ideas, but they stall because staff never have time to work on them. Which key activity of the continual improvement practice addresses this?
choices: Coordinating improvement activities across the organization
Measuring and evaluating improvement results
Securing time and budget for continual improvement
Logging opportunities in the improvement register
questions.explanation: The continual improvement practice includes securing time and budget for improvement, so that improvement work is resourced rather than squeezed out by daily work.

questions.prompt: A provider tracks improvement using measures from financial, customer, internal process and learning and growth perspectives. Which technique is this?
choices: SWOT analysis
Value stream mapping
Root cause analysis
Balanced scorecard
questions.explanation: A balanced scorecard measures performance from several perspectives, including financial, customer, internal processes and learning and growth. SWOT looks at strengths, weaknesses, opportunities and threats.

questions.prompt: Several teams launch improvement initiatives that overlap and conflict with each other. Which key activity of the continual improvement practice is MOST needed?
choices: Coordinating improvement activities across the organization
Securing time and budget for improvement
Making business cases for each improvement
Encouraging continual improvement across the organization
questions.explanation: Coordinating improvement activities across the organization ensures that initiatives do not duplicate or conflict with one another and that they support shared objectives.

questions.prompt: A service desk analyst notices a recurring delay in laptop deliveries and records it as a possible improvement for later assessment. Which continual improvement activity is this?
choices: Assessing and prioritizing improvement opportunities
Planning and implementing improvements
Identifying and logging improvement opportunities
Measuring and evaluating improvement results
questions.explanation: Improvement opportunities should be identified and logged, typically in a continual improvement register, before being assessed and prioritized.

questions.prompt: Before improving its practices, an organization compares them with a capability and maturity model to understand how developed they are. Which continual improvement technique is this?
choices: A balanced scorecard review
A business case
A maturity assessment
A post-implementation review
questions.explanation: A maturity assessment compares current practices with a defined model, giving a baseline of where the organization is now so improvement targets can be set.

questions.prompt: A team often restarts a web service using a well-understood, fully documented, low-risk procedure, and wants to stop raising a full change request each time. What should be done?
choices: Make it a pre-authorized standard change
Treat each restart as an emergency change
Treat each restart as an incident instead
Ask the CAB to approve each restart faster
questions.explanation: Standard changes are low risk, well understood and fully documented, and can be implemented without additional authorization. Their risk is assessed when the procedure is created.

questions.prompt: During an emergency change to stop a live outage, there is no time to complete the full change documentation. What does ITIL 4 allow?
choices: The change must wait until all documentation is done
Emergency changes never need any documentation at all
Some documentation may be completed afterwards
The change must first be reclassified as a standard change
questions.explanation: ITIL 4 says it may be acceptable to defer some documentation of an emergency change until after implementation, while still assessing and authorizing it as far as possible.

questions.prompt: According to ITIL 4, who typically forms a separate change authority for emergency changes?
choices: The full CAB, convened at its next scheduled meeting
The service desk agent who logged the related incident
A few senior managers who understand the business risks
Any technician who is available to implement the change
questions.explanation: There may be a separate change authority for emergency changes, typically a small number of senior managers who understand the business risks involved, so decisions can be made quickly.

questions.prompt: A team plans to remove an obsolete monitoring agent from 200 servers. According to the ITIL 4 definition, is this a change?
choices: Yes, as removal could affect services
No, because nothing new is being added
No, because monitoring agents are not services
Only if users will notice that it was removed
questions.explanation: A change is the addition, modification or removal of anything that could have a direct or indirect effect on services, so a removal falls within change enablement.

questions.prompt: What determines the roles that assess and authorize a particular normal change?
choices: The seniority of the person requesting it
The change model for that type of change
The day of the week it is scheduled
The number of users who will be affected
questions.explanation: Normal changes are assessed and authorized through change models based on the type of change, which define the roles involved, from rapid low-risk decisions to senior authority for major changes.

questions.prompt: How is a normal change typically initiated?
choices: By logging a service request in the portal
By the change authority adding it to the schedule
By a change request, manual or automated
By the service desk raising an incident record
questions.explanation: Normal changes are initiated by the creation of a change request, which may be created manually or automated. Standard changes are often initiated as service requests.

questions.prompt: An organization plans a major architectural change with very high risk and cost. Who might act as the change authority?
choices: An automated pipeline check with no human review
The engineer who will implement the change
The service desk manager on duty that day
A senior authority, possibly the board
questions.explanation: The change authority for normal changes depends on the change model. Low-risk changes may be authorized rapidly or by automation, while very major changes may need authority as senior as the board.

questions.prompt: What does ITIL 4 recommend for incident target resolution times?
choices: Set by each technician based on current workload
Hidden from users to avoid raising complaints
Agreed, documented and communicated to users
Identical for every type and priority of incident
questions.explanation: Target resolution times are agreed, documented and communicated to ensure that expectations are realistic, and incidents are prioritized using an agreed classification.

questions.prompt: When a new incident is logged, the service management tool suggests a known error with matching symptoms and its workaround. Which capability is being used?
choices: Automated change authorization by the tool
Automated closure of the related problem records
Automated escalation under a supplier contract
Automated matching to problems and known errors
questions.explanation: Incident records should be linked to related CIs, changes, problems and known errors, and modern tools can match incidents automatically to speed up diagnosis and resolution.

questions.prompt: Two incidents arrive together. One stops 200 call centre agents from taking orders; the other affects a single executive's desk phone. How should they be prioritized?
choices: By the seniority of the person reporting
In the order they were logged, first come first served
By whichever is quicker to resolve
By business impact using the agreed classification
questions.explanation: Incidents are prioritized using an agreed classification based on impact and urgency, so that those with the highest business impact are resolved first.

questions.prompt: A support engineer fixes a user's problem in two minutes and asks whether it is worth logging. What does ITIL 4 say?
choices: Only incidents longer than an hour need logging
Incidents fixed at first contact are not logged
Logging is optional when no SLA has been agreed
Log it, so all incidents meet expected times
questions.explanation: Incidents should be logged and managed to ensure they are resolved within times that meet customer and user expectations. Records also support problem management and improvement.

questions.prompt: Some incidents are resolved by users themselves through self-help. Why should the use of self-help be recorded?
choices: To charge users for the support they used
To close the related problem record
To support measurement and improvement
To trigger an emergency change
questions.explanation: ITIL 4 states that the use of specific self-help records should be captured for measurement and improvement activities.

questions.prompt: A hardware vendor warns a provider about a firmware defect that could cause outages, although no incidents have happened yet. Which phase of problem management does this information feed?
choices: Problem identification
Problem control
Error control
Major incident handling
questions.explanation: Problem identification includes analysing information received from suppliers and partners, as well as trend analysis and detection of recurring issues, to find actual and potential causes.

questions.prompt: Problem analysis finds the root cause of an outage, and also finds that slow escalation made the outage last much longer. What does ITIL 4 recommend?
choices: Consider all causes, including those that prolonged it
Record only the single technical root cause found
Pass the escalation issue to incident management only
Ignore the delay because the root cause is now known
questions.explanation: Problem analysis should consider all contributory causes, including causes that contributed to the duration and impact of incidents, not just those that made them happen.

questions.prompt: A known error is still unresolved, and after a recent upgrade its workaround has become less effective. Which phase of problem management regularly re-assesses known errors, including how well their workarounds work?
choices: Problem identification
Problem control
Incident resolution
Error control
questions.explanation: Error control manages problems in known error status and regularly re-assesses them, considering impact, the cost and risk of permanent solutions, and the effectiveness of workarounds.

questions.prompt: A team documents a workaround in a problem record before its analysis of the problem is complete. What does ITIL 4 say about this?
choices: It must wait until the root cause is confirmed
It is acceptable; it is reviewed and improved later
It is allowed only once a permanent fix is rejected
It needs change authority approval before recording
questions.explanation: Workarounds can be documented at any point and need not wait for problem analysis to be complete; an early workaround should be reviewed and improved as analysis progresses.

questions.prompt: ITIL 4 says problem management activities can be organized as a specific case of which other practice?
choices: Service level management
Risk management
Release management
Relationship management
questions.explanation: Problem management can be organized as a specific case of risk management, aiming to identify, assess and control risks in any of the four dimensions of service management.

questions.prompt: A problem's root cause has been identified as a memory leak, but the fix is not scheduled until next quarter. In ITIL 4 terms, what is this problem now?
choices: A major incident
A known error
A standard change
An event
questions.explanation: A known error is a problem that has been analysed but has not been resolved. Its workaround and status are managed in error control until a permanent fix is made.

questions.prompt: Monitoring shows that a disk in one node of a cluster has a fault that could cause outages, although no users have been affected yet. In ITIL 4 terms, what is this?
choices: An incident, because a component has failed
A problem, as it may cause incidents
A known error, because the fault is visible
A service request, as a disk must be replaced
questions.explanation: A problem is a cause, or potential cause, of one or more incidents. An incident requires an unplanned interruption or reduction in service quality.

questions.prompt: A test team finds a defect in a new release, and the business accepts the release going live with the defect. Which practice should record and manage this defect?
choices: Incident management
Problem management
Service request management
Relationship management
questions.explanation: Problem identification includes analysing information from internal software developers, test teams and project teams, so known defects in released software are managed as problems and known errors.

questions.prompt: A new employee needs to be given access to the shared finance folder. Which type of service request is this?
choices: A request for information
A request for a service delivery action
Feedback, a compliment or a complaint
A request for access to a resource
questions.explanation: ITIL 4 lists request types including service delivery actions, information, provision of a resource or service, access to a resource or service, and feedback, compliments and complaints.

questions.prompt: Users complain that laptop requests take forever, although every request is delivered within the agreed five days. What does ITIL 4 recommend?
choices: Set clear expectations for fulfilment times
Treat every laptop request as an incident
Remove the target so that complaints stop
Escalate every request to the change authority
questions.explanation: Service request management advises that user expectations of fulfilment times should be clearly set, based on what the organization can realistically deliver.

questions.prompt: A user requests extra cloud storage on the portal, and it is provisioned automatically within minutes with no human involvement. What does this illustrate?
choices: A standard change that needed CAB approval
A request automated end to end
An incident resolved by user self-help
A deployment completed by release management
questions.explanation: ITIL 4 notes that service requests should be standardized and automated as much as possible, and some can be fully automated from submission to fulfilment.

questions.prompt: A user asks for a custom software feature that the provider has never offered or agreed to provide. Is this a service request?
choices: No, only pre-agreed actions are requests
Yes, any request a user makes is a service request
Yes, as long as it is logged through the portal
No, it must be logged and managed as an incident
questions.explanation: A service request initiates a service action that has been agreed as a normal part of service delivery. New, undefined work is handled as demand, often through change, not request fulfilment.

questions.prompt: According to ITIL 4, what is service request management dependent on?
choices: A dedicated change advisory board for every single request
Well-designed processes supported by tracking and automation
Highly technical specialist staff working on the service desk
A separate SLA negotiated for every individual request type
questions.explanation: Service request management depends on well-designed processes and procedures, operationalized through tracking and automation tools to maximize efficiency.

questions.prompt: Callers to the service desk choose menu options on their phone keypad so their call reaches the right team. Which technology is this?
choices: A configuration management system
Remote access tools
Workforce management software
Interactive voice response (IVR)
questions.explanation: Intelligent telephony at the service desk can include computer-telephony integration, interactive voice response and automatic call distribution to route calls.

questions.prompt: Why is the focus of service desks shifting towards supporting people and the business rather than technical issues alone?
choices: Automation and less technical debt absorb technical work
Technical issues are now handled only by external suppliers
Service desks are no longer involved in handling incidents
ITIL 4 removed all incident handling from the service desk
questions.explanation: ITIL 4 states that with increased automation and the gradual removal of technical debt, the service desk focuses on supporting people and the business rather than simply technical issues.

questions.prompt: A company opens a staffed tech bar in its head office where employees can bring their devices for help in person. Which service desk channel is this?
choices: Service portal
Walk-in service desk
Live chat
Public discussion forum
questions.explanation: ITIL 4 lists walk-in service desks among the channels a service desk can use, alongside phone, portals and mobile apps, chat, email, messaging and forums.

questions.prompt: A service desk manager wants to review how agents handle calls and coach them on the quality of their interactions. Which service desk tool supports this?
choices: Call recording and quality control
Automatic call distribution
Configuration management system
Remote access and control tools
questions.explanation: Call recording and quality control tools let the service desk review interactions to improve quality. Automatic call distribution only routes calls to agents.

questions.prompt: Which statement describes the service desk's effect on how users see the service provider?
choices: It has little effect, as users judge only the technology
It matters only for users who report major incidents
It strongly shapes user experience and perception
It affects only the internal running costs of the provider
questions.explanation: ITIL 4 highlights that the service desk has a major influence on user experience and on how the service provider is perceived by its users.

questions.prompt: Before defining any SLA metrics, a service level manager holds open conversations with customers to understand their business and what success looks like for them. Which SLM activity is this?
choices: Operational metric reporting
Customer feedback surveys
Business metric reporting
Customer engagement
questions.explanation: Customer engagement involves initial listening, discovery and information capture, on which metrics, measurement and ongoing progress discussions can be based.

questions.prompt: Each time a ticket is closed, the user receives a short survey about that interaction. Which source of service level information is this?
choices: An operational metric from monitoring tools
A business metric from the customer
Customer engagement through discovery sessions
Customer feedback from an event-based survey
questions.explanation: Customer feedback can be gathered from event-based surveys, like those sent after a ticket closes, and from overall surveys.

questions.prompt: Which of these is an operational metric used in service level management?
choices: Insurance claims processed per hour
Incident response and fix times
Customer revenue growth this quarter
Patients discharged on time each day
questions.explanation: Operational metrics are low-level indicators such as system availability, incident response and fix times, request processing times and system response times.

questions.prompt: A service level report for an insurer shows the number of claims processed per hour using the claims service. Which kind of metric is this?
choices: An operational metric
A customer engagement record
A business metric
A warranty requirement
questions.explanation: Business metrics can be any business activity the customer deems useful or valuable and uses to gauge the success of the service, rather than technical measures.

questions.prompt: Which activity is part of how service level management ensures defined service levels are met?
choices: Authorizing changes to the services listed in the SLA
Collecting, analysing and reporting service metrics
Restoring normal service operation after each outage
Recording every configuration item and its relationships
questions.explanation: Service level management ensures the organization meets defined service levels through the collection, analysis, storage and reporting of relevant metrics for identified services.

questions.prompt: A provider reports server uptime and network uptime separately, yet customers still cannot complete their work. What does service level management provide that addresses this?
choices: Separate SLAs for each infrastructure part
End-to-end visibility of the whole service
Automatic closure of related incidents
More detailed component-level reports
questions.explanation: Service level management provides end-to-end visibility of the organization's services, focusing on the whole service and the customer's outcomes rather than individual components.

questions.prompt: Besides recording and reporting events, what does the monitoring and event management practice establish?
choices: The appropriate response to those events
The approval of changes needed to fix events
The service level targets agreed with customers
The financial value of every monitored component
questions.explanation: Monitoring and event management identifies and prioritizes events and establishes the appropriate response, including responding to conditions that could lead to faults or incidents.

questions.prompt: Which of these is MOST clearly an IT asset in ITIL 4 terms?
choices: An incident record in the tool
A known error record
A published change schedule
A purchased software licence
questions.explanation: An IT asset is any financially valuable component that can contribute to the delivery of an IT product or service, such as hardware and software licences.

questions.prompt: Can a service itself be treated as a configuration item?
choices: No, only hardware and software are CIs
No, only components inside a service are CIs
Only if the service has an IT asset value
Yes, services are also treated as CIs
questions.explanation: Service configuration management treats services as CIs too, which helps the organization understand how the CIs that contribute to each service work together.

questions.prompt: Besides software and infrastructure components, what may a release also include?
choices: Only the software code that has been changed
Only the items the CAB authorized that week
Documentation, training and updated processes
Only components that have no dependencies
questions.explanation: A release may include many infrastructure and application components, plus documentation, training for users or staff, updated processes or tools, and anything else required.

questions.prompt: A security team spends its whole budget on preventive controls and has no way to spot or recover from breaches. What does ITIL 4 advise?
choices: Keep spending only on preventive controls
Move the whole budget into incident management
Accept that breaches simply cannot be detected
Balance prevention, detection and correction
questions.explanation: Information security management needs a balance of prevention, detection of incidents that cannot be prevented, and correction to recover from them.

questions.prompt: Monitoring tools detect thousands of changes of state every hour. According to ITIL 4, which of these are events?
choices: Every change of state that the tools detect
Only the changes that go on to cause an incident
Only those significant for managing a service or CI
Only the changes that are reported by users
questions.explanation: An event is any change of state that has significance for the management of a service or other configuration item, so not every detected change counts as an event.

questions.prompt: A provider and customer agree that the payroll run must finish by 06:00 on 99 percent of pay days. In ITIL 4 terms, what is this target?
choices: A service offering
A service level
A known error
A change model
questions.explanation: A service level is one or more metrics that define expected or achieved service quality. Service levels are typically documented in an SLA.
